lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: Friends in Trouble
lessons.notes_html:
Story Summary

Raheel and Basit were close friends who studied in the same school. They played outside together - cricket, fishing and long walks in the forest. On weekends they went to the nearby canal for fishing. Basit usually caught more fish than Raheel and sometimes gave fish to Raheel because Raheel often failed to catch any.

One day the two nature lovers wandered deep into the dense, dangerous forest. They followed whatever caught their attention, lost their way, and worried because their parents and the villagers had warned them about dangerous beasts living there. Then a huge black bear came towards them.

Raheel, who was good at climbing trees, climbed a tree to save himself and told Basit to run. Basit did not know how to climb. He was paralyzed with fear and shocked that his friend would abandon him. He lay flat on the ground and stopped breathing so the bear would think he was dead. The bear smelled Basit, took him for dead and walked away without harming him.

Raheel came down and asked what the bear had done. Basit said the bear had whispered in his ear: do not trust a friend who leaves his friend at the time of danger. In fact bears cannot speak - the bear had only smelled Basit. Basit invented the reply to teach Raheel a lesson. Raheel had seen the way out from the top of the tree, so both friends reached home safely.

Word Meanings

  • sympathetic - kind to someone sad or hurt
  • nature lovers - those who enjoy nature
  • curious - wanted to know
  • wandered - walked around without any purpose
  • dense - thick
  • in vain - without any success
  • abandon - leave someone because staying is dangerous
  • paralyzed - unable to move
  • apologising - saying sorry
  • whisper - speak very softly
  • embarrassed - ashamed

Key Points

  • Basit was kind and helpful because his parents had always taught him to be kind, sympathetic, helpful and sincere. He always helped Raheel with homework and shared his fish.
  • Raheel was good at climbing trees because he had a tall tree in his house which he had been climbing from an early age.
  • They went for long walks in the forest because they liked listening to the birds chirping, watching the animals at play, and looking at the beautiful flowers.
  • At the time of danger Raheel climbed a tree to save himself and left Basit alone.
  • Raheel supposed the bear had whispered something because he had seen the bear bring its face close to Basit's head.

Central Idea

The best heading and the central idea of the story is: A friend in need is a friend indeed. A true friend stands by you in danger, while a selfish friend leaves you alone.

mcqs.q: What is the most suitable heading for the story of Raheel and Basit?
options: A friend in need is a friend indeed
mcqs.why: The story shows that a true friend helps in danger, so 'A friend in need is a friend indeed' fits its central lesson best.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'sympathetic' mean in the story?
options: Kind to someone sad or hurt
mcqs.why: Sympathetic means kind to someone sad or hurt, which is how Basit was taught to behave towards others.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'dense' mean?
mcqs.why: Dense means thick, and it describes the thick forest into which Raheel and Basit wandered.

mcqs.q: What does the phrase 'in vain' mean?
mcqs.why: In vain means without any success, that is, trying hard but getting no result from the effort.

mcqs.q: What does 'paralyzed' mean in the story?
mcqs.why: Paralyzed means unable to move, and Basit was paralyzed with fear when he saw the bear coming towards him.

mcqs.q: What does 'whisper' mean?
mcqs.why: To whisper means to speak very softly, which is what Basit said the bear had done in his ear.

mcqs.q: Where did Raheel and Basit study?
mcqs.why: Both friends studied in the same school, so the statement that they went to one school together is true.

mcqs.q: What did the two friends do at the nearby canal on weekends?
mcqs.why: On weekends they went to the nearby canal for fishing, and Basit usually caught more fish than Raheel.

mcqs.q: Why was Raheel good at climbing trees?
options: He had a tall tree at home and had climbed it since early childhood
He learned climbing in the forest that day
His teacher taught him at school
mcqs.why: Raheel had a tall tree in his house which he had been climbing from an early age, so climbing came easily to him.

mcqs.q: What kind of place was the forest they visited?
mcqs.why: The forest was dangerous because their parents and the villagers had warned them about dangerous beasts living there.

mcqs.q: How did the friends feel when they visited the forest?
mcqs.why: They felt curious in the forest and kept following whatever caught their attention, which made them lose their way.

mcqs.q: Why did Basit not climb a tree when the bear came?
options: He was not afraid of animals
He did not know how to climb a tree
He wanted to fight the bear
mcqs.why: Basit did not know how to climb a tree, unlike Raheel, so he had to find another way to save himself.

mcqs.q: What did Basit say the bear had whispered in his ear?
options: Trust a friend who leaves you in danger
Be honest with such a friend
Do not trust a friend who leaves his friend at the time of danger
Always climb a tree in danger
mcqs.why: Basit said the bear warned him not to trust a friend who leaves his friend at the time of danger, teaching Raheel a lesson.

mcqs.q: Why did Basit lie down on the ground and stop breathing?
options: He was tired and wanted to sleep
He wanted the bear to think he was dead so it would not touch him
He had fallen and hurt himself
mcqs.why: Basit held his breath and lay flat so the bear would think he was dead and leave him alone without harming him.

mcqs.q: Did the bear really speak to Basit?
options: Yes, the bear whispered a lesson
Yes, bears in that forest could speak
No, the bear only smelled Basit and Basit invented the reply
No, Raheel invented the whole story
mcqs.why: Bears cannot speak; the bear only smelled Basit and walked away, and Basit invented the reply to teach Raheel a lesson.

lessons.title: Speaking: Making Plans
lessons.notes_html:
About This Lesson

This lesson gives one model dialogue in which three friends - Ali, Sara and Bilal - make a plan together. Read it carefully as a pattern for speaking about making plans. There is only this one model dialogue in the lesson, so every point comes from it.

The Model Dialogue

  • Ali opens happily: Hurrah! The final exams are over. He asks: How about visiting the museum?
  • Sara likes the idea at once: Oh! It is a great idea! She says she was also thinking about it.
  • Bilal suggests something different: Why not go to a park?
  • Ali gives a reason for the museum: a visit to the museum will not only be fun but it will also help them in writing the report for their next year's project work.
  • Bilal agrees when he remembers: Oh yes! I remember, the teacher told us about it last week.
  • Sara closes in agreement: I think going to the museum is a great idea.

Key Points

  • The plan is made after the final exams are over.
  • A good suggestion can be made with 'How about visiting...?' and 'Why not go to...?'
  • Giving a useful reason - fun plus help with the project report - persuades the friend who suggested the park.
  • The dialogue ends with everyone agreeing to visit the museum.

mcqs.q: Who first suggests visiting the museum?
mcqs.why: Ali opens the dialogue by saying the final exams are over and asking how about visiting the museum.

mcqs.q: When do the friends make this plan?
options: After the final exams are over
At the start of the school year
mcqs.why: Ali begins with 'Hurrah! The final exams are over', so the plan to visit the museum is made after the exams.

mcqs.q: How does Sara react to the museum idea at first?
options: She says it is a great idea and she was also thinking about it
She says it is a bad idea
She suggests going to a park instead
mcqs.why: Sara immediately calls it a great idea and says she was also thinking about visiting the museum.

mcqs.q: What does Bilal suggest instead of the museum?
mcqs.why: Bilal puts forward a different plan by asking why not go to a park instead of the museum.

mcqs.q: What reason does Ali give for choosing the museum?
options: It is close to his house
It will be fun and will help with the report for next year's project work
It has a big park inside
The teacher ordered them to go
mcqs.why: Ali says the museum visit will not only be fun but will also help them write the report for next year's project work.

mcqs.q: Who told the friends about the project work?
mcqs.why: Bilal remembers that the teacher told them about the project work last week, which supports Ali's reason.

mcqs.q: When did the teacher tell them about the project work?
mcqs.why: Bilal says he remembers the teacher told them about the project work last week.

mcqs.q: How does the dialogue end?
options: The friends decide to go to a park
Sara agrees that going to the museum is a great idea
Ali goes to the museum alone
mcqs.why: Sara closes the dialogue by agreeing that going to the museum is a great idea, so all three accept the plan.

mcqs.q: Which phrase does Ali use to make his suggestion?
options: Why not go to a park?
I remember the teacher told us
I think it is a great idea
mcqs.why: Ali makes his suggestion with the phrase 'How about visiting the museum?', a common way to propose a plan.

mcqs.q: How many friends take part in the model dialogue?
mcqs.why: Three friends take part in the dialogue - Ali, Sara and Bilal - and together they agree on the museum plan.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Used To
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Points

We use used to + the base form of a verb to talk about a past habit - something that happened regularly in the past. Example from the book: Her brother used to open his shop early in the morning.

Examples From the Book

  • When I was a child I used to ride a bicycle.
  • Essa used to love mangoes.
  • Seema used to get up early in the morning.
  • When I was a child my father used to take care of me.
  • They used to visit historical places.
  • Our pet dog used to play with the children.
  • My grandfather used to tease everyone in the family.
  • His brother used to bite our guests.

More Model Sentences

  • My father used to drive us to school.
  • My mother used to make breakfast for us.
  • My uncle used to give us gifts on Eid.
  • The shopkeeper used to sell toys in our street.
  • My grandmother used to call us every evening.
  • My friend used to send me letters.
  • I used to receive cards on my birthday.

Key Points

  • After 'used to', always use the base verb: used to ride, used to visit, used to play.
  • 'Used to' shows a habit of the past, often starting with a past time phrase like 'When I was a child'.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: When I was a child I used to ___ a bicycle.
mcqs.why: The book completes this sentence with ride, because we ride a bicycle, giving 'I used to ride a bicycle'.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: Essa used to ___ mangoes.
mcqs.why: The book completes this sentence with love, giving 'Essa used to love mangoes' as a past liking.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: Seema used to ___ early in the morning.
mcqs.why: The book completes this sentence with get up, giving 'Seema used to get up early in the morning'.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: When I was a child my father used to ___ care of me.
mcqs.why: The book completes this sentence with take, because the fixed phrase is 'take care of' someone.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: They used to ___ historical places.
mcqs.why: The book completes this sentence with visit, giving 'They used to visit historical places'.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: Our pet dog used to ___ with the children.
mcqs.why: The book completes this sentence with play, giving 'Our pet dog used to play with the children'.

mcqs.q: According to the book, what did the grandfather use to do?
mcqs.why: The book says the grandfather used to tease everyone in the family, showing his regular past habit.

mcqs.q: According to the book, what did his brother use to do?
mcqs.why: The book completes the sentence with bite, giving 'His brother used to bite our guests'.

mcqs.q: What is the book's example sentence with 'open'?
options: Her brother used to open his shop early in the morning
My father used to open us to school
I used to open cards on my birthday
The shopkeeper used to open toys
mcqs.why: The book's example is 'Her brother used to open his shop early in the morning', showing a past habit with used to.

mcqs.q: Which sentence correctly shows a past habit with 'used to'?
options: My grandmother used to call us every evening
My grandmother used to called us every evening
My grandmother use to calls us every evening
My grandmother used to calling us every evening
mcqs.why: After used to we use the base form of the verb, so 'used to call us every evening' is the correct past-habit form.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Prepositions of Position
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Points

Prepositions of position tell us where something or someone is: on, under, in, at, near, outside, inside, above, below, behind, between.

Examples From the Book

  • Please put this book on the table.
  • Her shoes are under the bed.
  • My teacher is in the class.
  • A huge crowd is waiting outside the stadium.
  • Their house is near their school.
  • I have put the baby in the cot.
  • The train is at the station.
  • Murree is about 7000 ft. above the sea level.
  • The boys fell in the pond yesterday.
  • Let's go inside as it is going to rain.
  • Many minerals were found below the surface of the earth.
  • We can get most of the things that we need near our house.
  • The old man is resting under the tree as it is very hot.
  • I always keep my mobile phone on the top shelf.
  • Please go and see who is at the door.
  • The mouse is behind the log in the corner.

More Model Sentences

  • The cat is under the chair. My school is near my house. The ball is inside the box. Ali is standing behind me. The kite is above the roof. The garden is between the two houses.

mcqs.q: Please put this book ___ the table.
mcqs.why: The book uses on for something placed on a surface, giving 'Put this book on the table'.

mcqs.q: Her shoes are ___ the bed.
mcqs.why: The book places the shoes under the bed, because they are below and beneath the bed.

mcqs.q: A huge crowd is waiting ___ the stadium.
mcqs.why: The book says the crowd is waiting outside the stadium, meaning not inside the stadium building.

mcqs.q: Their house is ___ their school.
mcqs.why: The book uses near to show the house is close to the school, giving 'Their house is near their school'.

mcqs.q: The train is ___ the station.
mcqs.why: The book uses at for a point or place like a station, giving 'The train is at the station'.

mcqs.q: Murree is about 7000 ft. ___ the sea level.
mcqs.why: The book uses above because Murree is higher than sea level, about 7000 feet above it.

mcqs.q: The boys fell ___ the pond yesterday.
mcqs.why: The book says the boys fell in the pond, because they went into the water of the pond.

mcqs.q: Many minerals were found ___ the surface of the earth.
mcqs.why: The book uses below because the minerals were found under the surface of the earth.

mcqs.q: The mouse is ___ the log in the corner.
mcqs.why: The book places the mouse behind the log, meaning at the back of the log in the corner.

mcqs.q: I always keep my mobile phone ___ the top shelf.
mcqs.why: The book uses on because the phone rests on the surface of the top shelf.

lessons.title: Writing: A Paragraph
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

A paragraph has a topic sentence that gives the main idea, supporting sentences that give details and reasons, and a closing sentence that ends the paragraph. A mind map can be made first to plan the ideas before writing.

My Favourite Place - Model Paragraph

Topic sentence: My favourite place is my neighbourhood park. I like it for many reasons. Supporting points: It is near my house and has green grass, tall trees and colourful flowers. In the evening children play there and families sit on the benches. The air is fresh, and I feel happy and relaxed there. Closing sentence: In short, the park near my home is the place I love most because it is beautiful, peaceful and full of life.

My School - Model Paragraph

My school is near my house. It has clean classrooms, a big playground and a library. Our teachers are kind and teach us well. I love my school because I learn new things there every day. This paragraph is written after making a mind map.

Our Hospital - Model Paragraph

Our hospital is across the road from our street. Doctors and nurses help sick people there day and night. It has clean rooms and medicines for patients. We are lucky to have a good hospital near our homes. This paragraph is also written after making a mind map.

mcqs.q: What is the topic sentence of the paragraph on 'My Favourite Place'?
options: My favourite place is my neighbourhood park. I like it for many reasons
The air is fresh and I feel happy there
In short, the park is the place I love most
Children play there in the evening
mcqs.why: The topic sentence introduces the main idea: my favourite place is my neighbourhood park, and I like it for many reasons.

mcqs.q: According to the model paragraph, where is the favourite park?
options: Across the road from the street
mcqs.why: The supporting sentences say the park is near my house and has green grass, tall trees and colourful flowers.

mcqs.q: What can be seen in the favourite park in the evening?
options: Children playing and families sitting on benches
mcqs.why: The paragraph says that in the evening children play in the park and families sit on the benches.

mcqs.q: How does the writer feel in the park?
mcqs.why: The paragraph says the air is fresh and I feel happy and relaxed there, giving a reason for liking the park.

mcqs.q: What is the closing sentence about the park?
options: My favourite place is my neighbourhood park
In short, the park near my home is the place I love most because it is beautiful, peaceful and full of life
mcqs.why: The closing sentence sums up the paragraph: the park is loved most because it is beautiful, peaceful and full of life.

mcqs.q: What does the paragraph on 'My School' say the school has?
options: Clean classrooms, a big playground and a library
mcqs.why: The school paragraph says the school has clean classrooms, a big playground and a library for the students.

mcqs.q: Why does the writer love his school?
options: Because it is across the road
Because he learns new things there every day
Because the air is fresh there
mcqs.why: The writer loves his school because he learns new things there every day, as the closing line of that paragraph says.

mcqs.q: Where is the hospital in the model paragraph?
options: Across the road from our street
mcqs.why: The hospital paragraph begins by saying our hospital is across the road from our street.

mcqs.q: Who helps sick people in the hospital, according to the paragraph?
options: Doctors and nurses, day and night
mcqs.why: The paragraph says doctors and nurses help sick people in the hospital day and night.

mcqs.q: What should be made before writing the paragraphs on 'My School' and 'Our Hospital'?
mcqs.why: Both tasks ask pupils to make a mind map first and then write the paragraph, so ideas are planned before writing.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Presentation
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

A presentation outline has three parts: Beginning, Middle and End. The Beginning starts with a greeting and introduces the topic. The Middle gives the main points in order. The End sums up the speaker's belief or conclusion.

Sorting the Sentences - 'Why do people study?'

  • Beginning: (b) Greeting. (d) Studying or getting an education is important for a number of reasons.
  • Middle: (c) To begin with, studying is an exercise for the mind. (a) In addition, it can bring a change in your life. (f) Finally, studying and getting educated will help in national development.
  • End: (e) In other words, I believe that studying is very important for everyone.

Presentation Template - 'Why do people study?'

  • Beginning: Greet the audience; introduce the topic: people study for many reasons.
  • Middle: Studying is an exercise for the mind; it can bring a change in your life; studying and getting educated helps national development.
  • End: In other words, studying is very important for everyone.

Model Outline - 'Why is school important?'

  • Beginning: Greet the audience; introduce the topic: school is important for many reasons.
  • Middle: School teaches us reading, writing and good manners; we make friends and learn to work together; it prepares us for future jobs.
  • End: In short, school is very important for every child.

Other titles offered for an outline were 'Why is sunshine important?' and 'Why is rain important?'

mcqs.q: Which part of a presentation comes first?
mcqs.why: A presentation outline begins with the Beginning, which starts with a greeting and introduces the topic.

mcqs.q: What belongs in the Beginning of the presentation on studying?
options: In other words, I believe studying is very important
Greeting, and 'Studying or getting an education is important for a number of reasons'
Finally, studying will help in national development
In addition, it can bring a change in your life
mcqs.why: The Beginning holds the greeting and the introducing sentence that studying is important for a number of reasons.

mcqs.q: Where does 'To begin with, studying is an exercise for the mind' belong?
mcqs.why: This sentence gives a main point about studying, so it belongs in the Middle part of the outline.

mcqs.q: Where does 'In addition, it can bring a change in your life' belong?
mcqs.why: This sentence adds another main point about studying, so it belongs in the Middle of the presentation.

mcqs.q: Where does 'Finally, studying and getting educated will help in national development' belong?
mcqs.why: This sentence is listed among the main points, so it belongs in the Middle, as the final middle point.

mcqs.q: Which sentence forms the End of the presentation on studying?
options: Studying is an exercise for the mind
In other words, I believe that studying is very important for everyone
Studying is important for a number of reasons
mcqs.why: The End sums up the speaker's belief: in other words, studying is very important for everyone.

mcqs.q: In the template for 'Why do people study?', what should the speaker do in the Beginning?
options: Greet the audience and introduce the topic
mcqs.why: The template says the Beginning should greet the audience and introduce the topic: people study for many reasons.

mcqs.q: Which is a Middle point in the outline 'Why is school important?'
options: School teaches us reading, writing and good manners
In short, school is very important for every child
mcqs.why: Teaching reading, writing and good manners is a main point, so it belongs in the Middle of that outline.

mcqs.q: What is the End of the outline 'Why is school important?'
options: We make friends and learn to work together
It prepares us for future jobs
School is important for many reasons
In short, school is very important for every child
mcqs.why: The End sums up the outline with the conclusion that, in short, school is very important for every child.

mcqs.q: Which other titles were offered for developing an outline?
options: Why is sunshine important? and Why is rain important?
mcqs.why: The task offers three titles, and besides school the other choices are why sunshine is important and why rain is important.

lessons.title: Fun: Tongue Twister
lessons.notes_html:
About This Activity

This is a fun speaking activity from the book (section 1.6). Pupils recite tongue twisters as fast as they can. A tongue twister is a sentence that is hard to say quickly because similar sounds come again and again.

Tongue Twisters From the Book

  • Six swans swam swiftly southwards.
  • I scream, you scream, we all scream for ice cream.
  • Four furious friends fought for the phone.
  • Never trouble trouble till trouble troubles you.
  • Sheena leads Sheila needs.
  • Double bubble gum bubbles double.
  • The queen in green screamed.
  • Silly sheep, weep and sleep.

The Class Game

  • The class is divided into two groups named Quaid-e-Azam and Allama Iqbal.
  • A student picks a chit marked from A to H and recites that tongue twister fast.
  • A fast and correct recital earns one mark for the student's group.
  • The group with more marks wins the game.

mcqs.q: Which tongue twister is about swans?
mcqs.why: The swan tongue twister in the book is 'Six swans swam swiftly southwards', built on repeated s sounds.

mcqs.q: Complete the tongue twister: 'I scream, you scream, we all scream for ___.'
mcqs.why: The book's tongue twister ends with ice cream: we all scream for ice cream.

mcqs.q: Which tongue twister mentions friends fighting for a phone?
options: Never trouble trouble till trouble troubles you
Four furious friends fought for the phone
mcqs.why: The book's tongue twister about the phone is 'Four furious friends fought for the phone'.

mcqs.q: Complete the tongue twister: 'Never trouble trouble till trouble ___ you.'
mcqs.why: The book's line is 'Never trouble trouble till trouble troubles you', repeating the word trouble.

mcqs.q: Which tongue twister is about a queen?
mcqs.why: The book's queen tongue twister is 'The queen in green screamed', with green and screamed rhyming closely.

mcqs.q: Complete the tongue twister: 'Double bubble gum bubbles ___.'
mcqs.why: The book's tongue twister is 'Double bubble gum bubbles double', repeating the word double.

mcqs.q: What are the two groups named in the class tongue-twister game?
mcqs.why: In the class game the two groups are named Quaid-e-Azam and Allama Iqbal, after the two great leaders.

mcqs.q: In the game, what does a student pick before reciting?
options: A chit marked A to H
mcqs.why: A student picks a chit marked from A to H and then recites the tongue twister written for that letter.

mcqs.q: How many marks does a fast and correct recital earn for the group?
mcqs.why: The game rule says a fast and correct recital earns one mark for the student's group.

mcqs.q: How is the winner of the tongue-twister game decided?
options: The group that recites the longest twister wins
The group with more marks wins
mcqs.why: The group with more marks wins the game, so every correct fast recital helps the whole group.

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: My Blessed Beautiful Land
lessons.notes_html:
Poem Summary

The poem My Blessed Beautiful Land describes the natural beauty of Pakistan province by province in four stanzas. The poet praises the mountains, deserts, plains, rivers and ancient places, praises the people of each area, and prays in every stanza: Oh my Lord, keep them all safe and sound.

The Four Stanzas

StanzaProvince / AreaTwo Main FeaturesPeople
1Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Gilgit BaltistanSnow-crowned Karakoram; beautiful HindukushWarm and brave
2BalochistanBrown sands of the Kharan desert; lofty mountains with precious stones and mines full of mineralsFearless
3PunjabFertile plains and fields of grain; five mighty riversSimple
4SindhThe Indus delta; the ancient site of Mohen-jo-DaroSincere and resourceful

Word Meanings

  • spellbinding - holding one's attention completely; astound - surprise a lot; mighty - very high; snow-crowned - peaks covered with snow; safe and sound - in good condition.
  • browned - turned brown in colour; lofty - very high; precious - valuable; fearless - brave; abound - found in large numbers.
  • fertile - soil where crops grow well; plains - a large area of flat land; renowned - famous; tales - exciting stories; legends - old stories that may or may not be true; profound - having a great effect.
  • delta - the mouth of a river where it spreads out before entering the sea; mound - a small hill; ancient - very old; echoes - repeated sounds; resound - loud, deep sound; resourceful - good at finding new ways to do things.

Key Points

  • Picture matching: desert dunes at sunset = Stanza 2, green fields = Stanza 3, a dam with flowing water = Stanza 4, snow-covered mountains = Stanza 1.
  • Six qualities of the people are named: warm, brave, fearless, simple, sincere and resourceful. Two more qualities we can add are hospitable and hardworking.
  • The poet is proud of Pakistan. We know this because he calls it my blessed beautiful land, describes the beauty of every province, praises its people and prays for them.

mcqs.q: Which stanza matches the picture of desert dunes at sunset?
options: Stanza 3 - fertile plains and fields of grain
Stanza 4 - the Indus and its delta
mcqs.why: The desert dunes picture matches Stanza 2 because that stanza describes the brown sands of the Kharan desert in Balochistan.

mcqs.q: Which stanza matches the picture of snow-covered mountains?
mcqs.why: Snow-covered mountains match Stanza 1 because it describes the snow-crowned Karakoram in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Gilgit Baltistan.

mcqs.q: What does 'spellbinding' mean in Stanza 1?
mcqs.why: In Stanza 1 spellbinding means holding one's attention completely, describing how the beautiful mountain scenery captures the viewer fully.

mcqs.q: What does 'astound' mean?
mcqs.why: Astound means to surprise a lot, which is the vocabulary meaning given for the word in Stanza 1 of the poem.

mcqs.q: What does 'fertile' mean in Stanza 3?
options: Soil or land where crops grow well
A large area of flat land
An old story that may not be true
mcqs.why: Fertile means soil or land where crops grow well, which describes the rich plains of Punjab in Stanza 3 of the poem.

mcqs.q: What is a 'delta' in Stanza 4?
options: The mouth of a river where it spreads out before entering the sea
mcqs.why: A delta is the mouth of a river where it spreads out before entering the sea, as the Indus does in Sindh in Stanza 4.

mcqs.q: Which two mountain ranges are named in Stanza 1?
mcqs.why: Stanza 1 names the Karakoram and the Hindukush as the two great mountain ranges of the northern area described in the poem.

mcqs.q: Which desert is mentioned in the poem?
mcqs.why: The poem mentions the Kharan desert, whose brown sands are described in Stanza 2 about the province of Balochistan.

mcqs.q: Which ancient site is mentioned in the poem?
mcqs.why: Mohen-jo-Daro is the ancient site mentioned in the poem, located in Sindh and described in Stanza 4 with its echoes of ancient times.

mcqs.q: Which prayer is repeated in each stanza?
options: Oh my Lord, bless this fertile land
Oh my Lord, keep them all safe and sound
Oh my Lord, make our rivers mighty
Oh my Lord, crown our peaks with snow
mcqs.why: The line Oh my Lord, keep them all safe and sound is the prayer repeated at the end of each stanza of the poem.

mcqs.q: In Stanza 2, Balochistan is described with the Kharan desert and what else?
options: Lofty mountains with precious stones and mines full of minerals
mcqs.why: Stanza 2 describes Balochistan with the brown sands of the Kharan desert and lofty mountains with precious stones and mineral mines.

mcqs.q: How many rivers are mentioned for Punjab in Stanza 3?
mcqs.why: Stanza 3 says Punjab has five mighty rivers, along with fertile plains and fields of grain where simple people work.

mcqs.q: How are the people of Sindh described in Stanza 4?
mcqs.why: The people of Sindh in Stanza 4 are described as sincere and resourceful, living near the Indus delta and Mohen-jo-Daro.

mcqs.q: How many qualities of the people of Pakistan are mentioned in the poem?
mcqs.why: Six qualities are mentioned in the poem: warm, brave, fearless, simple, sincere and resourceful, one set for each area described.

mcqs.q: How do we know the poet is proud of Pakistan?
options: He wants to leave the country
He calls it 'my blessed beautiful land' and prays to keep it safe and sound
mcqs.why: We know the poet is proud because he calls Pakistan my blessed beautiful land, praises every province and its people, and prays for their safety.

lessons.title: Speaking: Agree or Disagree Politely
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

In English we agree and disagree politely. The three dialogues in this section - about the best player, about train travel, and about books - show expressions we can use without sounding rude.

Agreeing Politely

  • I agree with you.
  • That's right!
  • Exactly!
  • You are right. But I agree with A.

Disagreeing Politely

  • No, I don't think so.
  • I'm afraid, I disagree with both of you.
  • I beg to differ.

Words like I'm afraid and I beg to differ soften disagreement and keep the conversation friendly.

mcqs.q: Which expression is used to AGREE in Dialogue 2 about train travel?
options: I'm afraid, I disagree with both of you
mcqs.why: I agree with you is an agreeing expression used in Dialogue 2 about train travel, along with That's right and Exactly.

mcqs.q: Which expression shows DISAGREEMENT in Dialogue 1 about the best player?
mcqs.why: No, I don't think so is used to disagree politely in Dialogue 1 about the best player, without sounding rude to others.

mcqs.q: What does 'I'm afraid, I disagree with both of you' express?
mcqs.why: I'm afraid, I disagree with both of you expresses polite disagreement in Dialogue 1, where I'm afraid softens the disagreement.

mcqs.q: Which phrase means the same as a polite 'I disagree' in Dialogue 3 about books?
mcqs.why: I beg to differ is the polite disagreeing expression in Dialogue 3 about books, used instead of saying bluntly that someone is wrong.

mcqs.q: 'That's right!' and 'Exactly!' in Dialogue 2 are used to:
mcqs.why: That's right and Exactly are used to agree strongly in Dialogue 2 about train travel, showing full support for what was said.

mcqs.q: In Dialogue 3, 'You are right. But I agree with A.' shows the speaker is:
mcqs.why: You are right. But I agree with A shows agreeing in Dialogue 3, accepting one point while supporting A's opinion on books.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a DISAGREEING expression?
mcqs.why: I beg to differ is a disagreeing expression from Dialogue 3, while the other choices are all expressions used for agreeing.

mcqs.q: Dialogue 1 about the best player mainly contains expressions for:
mcqs.why: Dialogue 1 about the best player mainly contains disagreeing expressions: No, I don't think so and I'm afraid, I disagree with both of you.

mcqs.q: Dialogue 2 about train travel mainly contains expressions for:
mcqs.why: Dialogue 2 about train travel mainly contains agreeing expressions: I agree with you, That's right and Exactly.

mcqs.q: Why do we add words like 'I'm afraid' before disagreeing?
options: To make disagreement sound polite and soft
mcqs.why: We add I'm afraid before disagreeing to make disagreement sound polite and soft, as shown in Dialogue 1 about the best player.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Past Perfect Tense
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Points

The Past Perfect Tense is used for the action that happened first (earlier) when two past actions are mentioned. The later action uses the Simple Past.

  • Form: had + past participle - e.g. had studied, had lost, had watched, had worked, had read, had finished, had gone, had left, had stopped.
  • Example: I had studied Japanese before I went to study in Japan. Studying happened first.
  • Example: The train had left when we reached because we were late. The train leaving happened first.
  • Example: We went out for a walk after it had stopped raining. The rain stopping happened first.

Key Points

  • Words like before and after often join the two actions.
  • In the race story, the past perfect shows earlier actions: their friend had fallen down; she had injured herself; she had hurt her knee.
  • The lesson of the race story is that helping others and caring for their feelings is as important as winning a competition.

mcqs.q: In 'I studied Japanese before I went to study in Japan', which action happened FIRST?
mcqs.why: Studying Japanese happened first, so it takes the past perfect: I had studied Japanese before I went to study in Japan.

mcqs.q: What is the correct form? 'We had trouble at the airport because we ___ our passports.'
mcqs.why: Losing the passports happened first, so the past perfect had lost is correct: we had lost our passports before the trouble.

mcqs.q: In 'After we watched TV for a while we went to sleep', which action happened first?
mcqs.why: Watching TV happened first, so we say: After we had watched TV for a while we went to sleep, using had watched.

mcqs.q: Sachal knew many people at the office because he ___ there some years ago.
mcqs.why: Working there happened first and earlier, so the past perfect had worked is used: he had worked there some years ago.

mcqs.q: Farah enjoyed the movie because she ___ the book.
mcqs.why: Reading the book happened before enjoying the movie, so the past perfect had read correctly shows the earlier action.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct sentence for the homework example?
options: I had played cricket after I finish my homework
I played cricket after I had finished my homework
I play cricket after I had finished my homework
I had played cricket after I had finish my homework
mcqs.why: Finishing homework happened first, so it is had finished, and the later action played is in the simple past tense.

mcqs.q: 'When I came to your house last night you ___ to bed.' Choose the past perfect form.
mcqs.why: Going to bed happened before the speaker came, so the past perfect had gone is correct for the earlier action.

mcqs.q: 'The train ___ the station when we reached because we were late.'
mcqs.why: The train leaving happened first, before reaching the station, so the past perfect had left is the correct form here.

mcqs.q: 'We went out for a walk after it ___ raining.'
mcqs.why: The rain stopping happened first, so the past perfect had stopped is used before the later action went out.

mcqs.q: What is the form of the Past Perfect Tense?
mcqs.why: The Past Perfect Tense is formed with had plus the past participle, for example had studied, had lost and had gone.

mcqs.q: In the race story, why did the girls stop running?
options: One of their friends was crying because she had fallen down
mcqs.why: In the race story the girls stopped because one friend was crying; they turned and saw that she had fallen down earlier.

mcqs.q: In the race story: 'When they reached her, they saw that she ___ herself.'
mcqs.why: Injuring herself happened before the girls reached her, so the story uses the past perfect: she had injured herself.

mcqs.q: What did the two girls do for their injured friend in the race story?
options: Picked her up and waited till she steadied herself
Ran to the finishing line alone
mcqs.why: Two girls picked her up and waited till she steadied herself, then all held hands and ran to the finishing line together.

mcqs.q: What powerful lesson did the girls teach everyone in the race story?
options: Helping others and caring for their feelings is as important as winning
mcqs.why: The girls taught that helping others and caring for their feelings is as important as winning a competition, and everyone clapped.

mcqs.q: 'My father ___ to Syria before the problems started in that country.'
mcqs.why: Being in Syria happened first, before the problems started, so the past perfect had been is the correct form.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Prepositions of Movement
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Points

Prepositions of movement show direction: towards, from, to, up, down, across, through, along, around, into.

  • across - running across the road; along - planted all along the street; walked along the row of shelves.
  • up - climbed up the ladder; went up the stairs. down - fell down the stairs; looked up and down the road.
  • to - going to Gilgit; went to the manager's room. from - come from Quetta; walking home from my office.
  • around - turned around the corner. into - dived into the water; stepped into the lift. through - walk through this tunnel; walking through the door. towards - walking towards my friend; a man coming towards me.

Key Points

In the model paragraph: Yesterday I was walking home from school. A dog came running towards me from across the road. I looked up and down the street and ran through the gate into our house. I walked along the corridor and went up the stairs to my room.

mcqs.q: The boy looked left and right before running ___ the road.
mcqs.why: Across is correct because the boy runs from one side of the road to the other: running across the road.

mcqs.q: Many trees have been planted all ___ the street.
mcqs.why: Along is correct because the trees are planted in a line beside the street: planted all along the street.

mcqs.q: The fireman climbed ___ the ladder to rescue the old lady.
mcqs.why: Up is correct because the fireman moves to a higher place on the ladder: climbed up the ladder to rescue her.

mcqs.q: Saleha's aunt has come ___ Quetta to visit them.
mcqs.why: From is correct because Quetta is the starting place of the journey: she has come from Quetta to visit them.

mcqs.q: The swimmer dived ___ the water from a height of 100 ft.
mcqs.why: Into is correct because the swimmer moves from outside to inside the water: dived into the water from a height.

mcqs.q: Walk ___ this tunnel to get to the other side.
mcqs.why: Through is correct because walking through the tunnel means moving inside it from one end to the other side.

mcqs.q: Rustam fell ___ the stairs and broke his leg.
mcqs.why: Down is correct because Rustam fell from a higher to a lower place: fell down the stairs and broke his leg.

mcqs.q: In the story, the man was seen walking ___ the door.
mcqs.why: Through is correct in the story because the man entered by passing through the door of the shop after the narrator.

mcqs.q: I walked ___ the row of shelves, stepped ___ the lift.
mcqs.why: Along fits moving beside the row of shelves, and into fits entering the lift: walked along the row, stepped into the lift.

mcqs.q: My brother is going ___ Gilgit next week, and the boy turned ___ the corner.
mcqs.why: To shows destination in going to Gilgit, and around shows turning at the corner: turned around the corner and stopped.

lessons.title: Writing: An Application
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

An application to the Principal is a formal short letter. It has: date, The Principal with school name, a greeting Respected Sir/Madam, the reason in polite words, the request, thanks, and a closing with name and class.

Leave Application

  • Dated November 14, 2017, to The Principal, Govt. High School, Jamshoro.
  • Reason: my sister is getting married next week.
  • Request: grant leave for two days, from 20th November to 21st November 2017, to attend the wedding.
  • Polite lines: With due respect; I shall be very thankful to you; Thanking you in anticipation.
  • Closing: Yours Sincerely, (Your Name), Class VIII.

Study Tour Application

  • Dated March 25, 2017, to The Principal, XYZ School, Karachi. Subject: Request for allowing the Class VIII students to go on a study tour.
  • Place: the Sindh Museum, Hyderabad. Day and time: Monday, April 2, at 8 a.m., return by 5 p.m.
  • Four teachers have agreed to go with the students, and students will follow all school rules.
  • Closing: Yours Obediently, Students of Class VIII.

mcqs.q: In the leave application, why does the student ask for leave?
options: Because his/her sister is getting married
mcqs.why: The leave application asks for leave because the student's sister is getting married next week and the student must attend the wedding.

mcqs.q: For how many days is leave requested in the leave application?
mcqs.why: Leave is requested for two days, from 20th November to 21st November 2017, so the student can attend the sister's wedding.

mcqs.q: To whom is the leave application addressed?
options: The Principal, Govt. High School, Jamshoro
mcqs.why: The leave application is addressed to The Principal, Govt. High School, Jamshoro, dated November 14, 2017, as in the model.

mcqs.q: Which closing is used in the leave application?
options: Yours Obediently, Students of Class VIII
Yours Sincerely, with name and Class VIII
mcqs.why: The leave application closes with Yours Sincerely, followed by the student's name and Class VIII, after thanking the Principal.

mcqs.q: What is the subject of the study tour application?
options: Request for allowing the Class VIII students to go on a study tour
mcqs.why: The study tour application's subject is Request for allowing the Class VIII students to go on a study tour to the Sindh Museum.

mcqs.q: Where do the Class VIII students want to go on the study tour?
mcqs.why: The students want to go on a study tour to the Sindh Museum, Hyderabad, to learn from the visit before the new term.

mcqs.q: When will the study tour go and return?
options: Monday, April 2, at 8 a.m., return by 5 p.m.
Friday, at 10 a.m., return next day
mcqs.why: The tour will go on Monday, April 2, at 8 a.m. and will return by 5 p.m. on the same day, as stated in the application.

mcqs.q: How many teachers have agreed to go with the students on the study tour?
mcqs.why: Four teachers have agreed to go with the Class VIII students on the study tour, if the Principal allows the visit.

mcqs.q: Which polite phrase appears in both model applications?
options: With due respect I play cricket
mcqs.why: Thanking you in anticipation appears in both model applications as a polite closing line before Yours Sincerely or Yours Obediently.

mcqs.q: In the study tour application, what do the students promise?
options: To follow all the school rules
mcqs.why: The students promise to follow all the school rules during the study tour, as written in their application to the Principal.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Checklist
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

Section 2.5 asks: What kind of study habits do you have? Put a check mark against each thing that you do most of the time.

  • I always sit in one place to study or to do my homework.
  • I have a special place to study that is comfortable and quiet.
  • I keep all my study materials in one place including paper, pencils, pens, dictionary, etc.
  • I study at about the same time every day, and know that this is the best time for me.
  • When I sit down to study, I first decide what I will do and in which order I will study; maths first or English.
  • I also decide whether I will do all the work at one time or do some work now and some later.
  • I usually have enough time to finish my homework.
  • I can contact at least one person in my class if I have a question about an assignment.
  • I always do some reading for fun and enjoyment.
  • I check my bag every night to see that I have all my books and other things that I will need in class the next day.

Then work with a partner, prepare a list of things you should do but don't, and number them in the order you plan to change those habits.

mcqs.q: What does the Study Skills checklist ask you to put against each thing you do most of the time?
mcqs.why: The checklist says to put a check mark against each thing that you do most of the time when studying or doing homework.

mcqs.q: According to the checklist, where should you keep all your study materials?
mcqs.why: The checklist says to keep all study materials in one place, including paper, pencils, pens, dictionary and other items.

mcqs.q: What kind of special place to study does the checklist describe?

mcqs.q: When should you study, according to the checklist?

At about the same time every day

mcqs.q: When you sit down to study, what should you first decide?

mcqs.why: When you sit down to study, first decide what you will do and in which order you will study, for example maths first or English.

mcqs.q: What should you decide about doing all the work?
