lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: Better Be Safe Than Sorry
lessons.notes_html:
Text Summary

The text Better Be Safe Than Sorry has 6 paragraphs. It explains that many people die or are injured in road accidents because people do not follow road safety rules. Pedestrians cross roads carelessly and do not use footpaths. Motorcyclists drive fast and do not wear helmets. Children play in the streets, and beggars and people selling different things walk on the roads.

People should be taught road safety rules in different ways. Radio and television can teach through interesting programmes. Schools can have traffic education programmes. Parents should not allow under-age children to drive cars or motorcycles. Textbooks can teach simple rules like the Green Cross Code and walking on the footpath, or on the side of the road if there is no footpath.

Main Idea of Each Paragraph

  • Paragraph 1: Road accidents happen because people do not follow traffic rules.
  • Paragraph 2: Three types of people are responsible for most accidents.
  • Paragraph 3: The role of the media, school and traffic police.
  • Paragraph 4: The role of parents in road safety.
  • Paragraph 5: Textbooks and road safety.
  • Paragraph 6: Safety tips for road users.

Safety Tips Table

The table gives safety tips for 4 types of road users: cyclists, pedestrians, school/public transport users and motorcycle pillion riders. For each type there are 6 tips in total — 3 things they must do and 3 things they should not do.

Road usersTips for each type
Cyclists, pedestrians, school/public transport users, pillion riders6 tips: 3 must do + 3 should not do

Word Meanings

  • undisciplined — breaking rules.
  • pedestrians — people who use the road for walking.
  • stunts — actions that are often dangerous.
  • dodging — walking in and out of moving traffic.
  • strategies — different ways of doing things.
  • appealing — programmes that people always like to watch.
  • under-age — for driving a car, less than 18 years old.
  • impart — to provide education.
  • reflectors — things that shine when light falls on them.
  • pillion riders — people who sit behind the driver on a cycle or motorbike.
  • dangle — to hang feet in the air.
  • distract — to take away someone's attention.

Key Points

  • If we follow traffic rules, we can prevent deaths and injuries on the road.
  • Careless pedestrians are responsible for many recorded road accidents.
  • Many motorcyclists ride too fast — they are not all careful and slow.
  • Awareness does not come only from traffic laws. It also comes through media, schools, police, parents and textbooks.
  • The media can teach not only through news but also through appealing radio and TV programmes.
  • Both parents and schools have a duty to teach about road safety.
  • Green Cross Code: Stop, look, listen, think and cross.
  • Cyclists have their own set of safety rules. Bus users must also follow rules.
  • Zebra crossings are safe points for crossing roads.
  • Cyclists should stay on the extreme left. Pedestrians should wait patiently and cross when it is safe. People should not get off moving vehicles.

mcqs.q: How many paragraphs does the text 'Better Be Safe Than Sorry' have?
mcqs.why: The text has 6 paragraphs. The exercise asks for the total number of paragraphs, and the book's answer is 6, with safety tips given in paragraph 6.

mcqs.q: For how many types of road users does the safety tips table give tips?
mcqs.why: The table covers 4 types of road users: cyclists, pedestrians, school/public transport users and motorcycle pillion riders. That is why 4 is the correct count.

mcqs.q: How many tips does the table give for each type of road user?
options: 4 tips: 2 must do and 2 should not do
5 tips: 3 must do and 2 should not do
6 tips: 3 must do and 3 should not do
6 tips: 4 must do and 2 should not do
mcqs.why: Each type gets 6 tips in total, made up of 3 things they must do and 3 things they should not do. The equal 3 and 3 split is the key point of the table.

mcqs.q: People who display undisciplined behaviour usually do what?
mcqs.why: Undisciplined behaviour means breaking rules. People who are undisciplined do not maintain or follow rules, so breaking rules is the correct meaning here.

mcqs.q: Pedestrians are people who use the road for what?
mcqs.why: Pedestrians are people who walk on the road. The word is about walking, not driving or racing, which is why pedestrians must use footpaths and zebra crossings.

mcqs.q: Stunts are actions that are often what?
mcqs.why: Stunts are dangerous actions. The text warns against performing stunts on the road because such dangerous actions can cause serious accidents.

mcqs.q: Beggars who can be seen dodging traffic are the ones who do what?
options: walk in and out of moving traffic
mcqs.why: Dodging traffic means walking in and out of moving traffic. It does not mean stopping traffic, but moving dangerously between moving vehicles.

mcqs.q: Different strategies can be used means we can use different what?
mcqs.why: Strategies means ways of doing things. Teachers and others can use different strategies, that is different ways, to teach road safety well.

mcqs.q: Appealing programmes are programmes that people do what?
mcqs.why: Appealing programmes are programmes people always like to watch. Because they are attractive, the media can use them to teach road safety in an interesting way.

mcqs.q: For driving a car, under-age children are those less than what age?
mcqs.why: Under-age for driving a car means less than 18 years old. Parents must not allow children below this age to drive cars or motorcycles.

mcqs.q: Which paragraph gives safety tips for road users?
mcqs.why: Paragraph 6 gives safety tips for road users. The matching exercise places safety tips at the end of the text, after the roles of media, parents and textbooks.

mcqs.q: What is the Green Cross Code?
options: Cross, think and run at once
Stop, look, listen, think and cross
mcqs.why: The Green Cross Code is stop, look, listen, think and cross. Remembering all five steps in order helps pedestrians cross the road safely.

mcqs.q: What is the main idea of Paragraph 4?
options: The role of parents in road safety
mcqs.why: Paragraph 4 is about the role of parents in road safety. Parents teach children safe habits and must not let under-age children drive.

mcqs.q: Which statement about cyclists is true according to the text?
options: Cyclists have no rules at all
Cyclists must not follow any rules
Cyclists have their own set of safety rules
Cyclists can ride anywhere they like
mcqs.why: Cyclists have their own set of safety rules, so the statement that they have no rules is false. Every road user, including cyclists and bus users, must follow rules.

mcqs.q: Passengers who distract the drivers do what to them?
mcqs.why: To distract means to take away someone's attention. If passengers distract the driver, the driver cannot concentrate and an accident can happen.

lessons.title: Speaking: Expressing Opinion
lessons.notes_html:
About This Lesson

This is a thin lesson. It is built only from three speaking tasks: advice to a pillion rider, a suggestion for a brother who walks home, and a model dialogue for expressing opinion about mobile phones in schools.

Advice to a Motorcyclist — As a Pillion Rider

  • Please do not drive fast; drive slowly and carefully.
  • Please do not perform stunts on the road.

Suggestion for a Brother Who Walks Home

Always walk on the footpath, and use the zebra crossing and the Green Cross Code — stop, look, listen, think and cross — to cross the road.

Expressing Opinion — Model Dialogue

Ahmed: What do you think about using mobile phones in schools?

Sameer: I think it is a good idea! Phones can help us learn. What do you say, Nadeem?

Nadeem: I like it, but I think phones can disturb our studies.

Sameer: What is your opinion, Ahmed?

Ahmed: Well, I think phones are useful if we use them only for learning. But, yes, we must not use them in class without the teacher's permission.

Nadeem: Yes, that's right. I agree with you.

Useful Expressions

  • Asking opinion: What do you think about...? / What do you say...? / What is your opinion...?
  • Giving opinion: I think... / I like it, but I think...
  • Agreeing: Yes, that's right. I agree with you.

Key Points

  • Sameer supports phones because they can help students learn.
  • Nadeem agrees partly, but warns that phones can disturb studies.
  • Ahmed's balanced view: phones are useful only for learning, and never in class without the teacher's permission.

mcqs.q: As a pillion rider, what is the first piece of advice in the model answer?
options: Please do not drive fast; drive slowly and carefully
Please drive as fast as possible
Please talk to passengers while driving
mcqs.why: The model advice tells the motorcyclist not to drive fast, but to drive slowly and carefully. Slow and careful driving keeps both rider and pillion rider safe.

mcqs.q: What is the second piece of advice given to the motorcyclist?
options: Please wear dark clothes at night
Please do not perform stunts on the road
Please use the footpath for riding
mcqs.why: The second advice is not to perform stunts on the road. Stunts are dangerous actions, so the pillion rider asks the motorcyclist to avoid them completely.

mcqs.q: A brother who walks home from work should always walk where?
options: In the middle of the road
On the rooftop of a bus
mcqs.why: He should always walk on the footpath. Walking on the footpath keeps a pedestrian away from moving traffic and greatly reduces the risk of an accident.

mcqs.q: How should the brother cross the road to remain safe?
options: By using the zebra crossing and the Green Cross Code
mcqs.why: He should use the zebra crossing and the Green Cross Code — stop, look, listen, think and cross. These two safe methods together are the model suggestion in the lesson.

mcqs.q: What are the steps of the Green Cross Code mentioned in this lesson?
options: Stop, look, listen, think and cross
Stop, run and cross at once
mcqs.why: The Green Cross Code is stop, look, listen, think and cross. The brother is advised to follow all five steps every time he crosses the road.

mcqs.q: Who asks the first question in the mobile phones dialogue?
mcqs.why: Ahmed asks the first question: 'What do you think about using mobile phones in schools?' He starts the discussion and later gives his own balanced opinion as well.

mcqs.q: What is Sameer's opinion about mobile phones in schools?
options: It is a bad idea in every way
Phones should be banned at home
It is a good idea because phones can help us learn
Phones have no use for students
mcqs.why: Sameer thinks it is a good idea because phones can help students learn. His positive opinion is the first opinion expressed in the dialogue.

mcqs.q: What warning does Nadeem give about mobile phones?
options: Phones are too heavy to carry
Phones are useful only for games
mcqs.why: Nadeem likes the idea but warns that phones can disturb studies. His view balances Sameer's support by pointing out a real disadvantage of phones in school.

mcqs.q: According to Ahmed, when are phones useful in school?
options: When they are used during every lesson
When they are used only for learning
When they are used without any rules
When they are used for playing games
mcqs.why: Ahmed says phones are useful if they are used only for learning. This condition is the centre of his opinion and is what Nadeem finally agrees with.

mcqs.q: When must students not use phones in class, according to Ahmed?
options: When the teacher is speaking loudly
When they are sitting with friends
mcqs.why: Ahmed says students must not use phones in class without the teacher's permission. Permission from the teacher is the rule that makes phone use acceptable in class.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Must and Must Not
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Points

Must shows something necessary or a duty that we have to do. Mustn't (must not) shows something that is not allowed or that we should never do.

Must Do and Mustn't Do — For Students

Must DoMustn't Do
Exercise regularly; study hard; obey their teachers; follow the school rules; do their homeworkBehave rudely; shout in class; break the school furniture; miss their classes; write on the school wall or furniture

Model Sentences with Must / Mustn't

  • A good friend must help his friends in need. A good friend mustn't leave his friend in danger.
  • A good teacher must teach honestly and kindly. A good teacher mustn't punish students unfairly.
  • A good classmate must cooperate with everyone. A good classmate mustn't tease others.
  • A good brother or sister must care for the younger ones. A good brother or sister mustn't fight without reason.
  • A good parent must look after the children and teach them good manners. A good parent mustn't allow under-age children to drive.
  • A good son or daughter must obey and respect parents. A good son or daughter mustn't disobey parents.
  • A good neighbour must help neighbours in need. A good neighbour mustn't quarrel with neighbours.
  • A good citizen must follow the traffic rules and the law. A good citizen mustn't break the law.

Problems in Our Surroundings

ProblemMust DoMustn't Do
Garbage around the houseTalk to the people to find a solution; put garbage in dustbins and keep the area cleanThrow garbage around the house; leave garbage on the streets
Wastage of waterTurn off taps after use; get leaking taps fixedLeave taps running; waste clean water
Air pollutionPlant more trees; keep vehicles in good conditionBurn plastic and garbage; blow horns unnecessarily

Model Speech

Good morning, everyone! Our group found three problems in our surroundings: garbage around the house, wastage of water, and air pollution. We must put garbage in dustbins, save water and plant trees. We mustn't throw garbage on the streets, waste clean water, or burn plastic. If we all follow these rules, our surroundings will become clean and healthy. Thank you!

mcqs.q: Which of these belongs in the MUST DO list for students?
mcqs.why: Exercise regularly belongs in the must do list because it is a healthy duty for students. Behaving rudely, shouting and breaking furniture are all in the mustn't do list.

mcqs.q: Which of these belongs in the MUSTN'T DO list for students?
options: Write on the school wall or furniture
mcqs.why: Writing on the school wall or furniture must not be done, so it belongs in the mustn't do list. Studying, homework and obeying teachers are all must do actions.

mcqs.q: Complete the model sentence: A good friend must...
mcqs.why: A good friend must help his friends in need. This positive duty uses must, while leaving a friend in danger is what a good friend mustn't do.

mcqs.q: Complete the model sentence: A good teacher mustn't...
mcqs.why: A good teacher mustn't punish students unfairly. Teaching honestly and kindly is what a good teacher must do, so unfair punishment is the forbidden action.

mcqs.q: Complete the model sentence: A good parent mustn't...
mcqs.why: A good parent mustn't allow under-age children to drive. This links the grammar lesson back to road safety, where under-age driving is a cause of accidents.

mcqs.q: Complete the model sentence: A good citizen must...
options: Follow the traffic rules and the law
mcqs.why: A good citizen must follow the traffic rules and the law. Following rules is the citizen's duty, while breaking the law is what a good citizen mustn't do.

mcqs.q: For the problem of garbage around the house, what must we do?
options: Put garbage in dustbins and keep the area clean
mcqs.why: For garbage, we must put garbage in dustbins and keep the area clean, and talk to people to find a solution. Throwing garbage on streets is in the mustn't do column.

mcqs.q: For the problem of wastage of water, what mustn't we do?
mcqs.why: We mustn't leave taps running, because that wastes water. Turning off taps after use and fixing leaking taps are the must do actions for this problem.

mcqs.q: For the problem of air pollution, what must we do?
mcqs.why: We must plant more trees and keep vehicles in good condition to fight air pollution. Burning plastic and blowing horns unnecessarily are mustn't do actions.

mcqs.q: According to the model speech, what will happen if we all follow these rules?
options: Our surroundings will become clean and healthy
mcqs.why: The speech ends by saying our surroundings will become clean and healthy if we all follow these rules. That hopeful result is the conclusion of the whole must and mustn't plan.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Imperative Sentences
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Points

Imperative sentences give instructions, orders or directions. They usually begin with the base form of a verb, without a subject, for example: Take, Separate, Wash, Apply, Scrub, Rinse, Dry, Keep. Instructions are written in the correct order, step by step.

Washing Dishes — Instructions in Order

  • 1. Take all the utensils, glasses, dishes etc. to the washing area.
  • 2. Separate them into different piles.
  • 3. Wash the small things, like spoons, bowls and things made of glass first.
  • 4. Apply soap to all the things mentioned above and then rinse them with water.
  • 5. Scrub all the other utensils properly using the washing powder and soap.
  • 6. Rinse all the scrubbed utensils one by one.
  • 7. Dry them with a clean towel.
  • 8. Keep them in their proper place.

Making Tea — Instructions

  • 1. Take a kettle and fill it with water.
  • 2. Put the kettle on the stove and heat the water.
  • 3. Add tea leaves and boil the water.
  • 4. Add milk and sugar and stir well.
  • 5. Pour the tea into cups.
  • 6. Put the cups on a tray with biscuits.
  • 7. Serve the tea to the guests.

Action words used for tea: boil, pour, stir, add, take, heat, put, serve, fill.

Rules Students Must Follow in Class

  • Wear neat and clean uniforms.
  • Come to class on time.
  • Listen to the teacher quietly.
  • Raise your hand before speaking.
  • Keep the classroom clean.
  • Do your homework regularly.

mcqs.q: What is the first step in washing dishes?
options: Take all the utensils to the washing area
Dry them with a clean towel
Keep them in their proper place
mcqs.why: The first step is to take all the utensils, glasses and dishes to the washing area. Drying, keeping and rinsing all come later in the correct order.

mcqs.q: After taking the utensils, what should you do next?
mcqs.why: Next you separate them into different piles. Separating comes before washing, so the small things can be washed first in an organised way.

mcqs.q: Which things should be washed first when washing dishes?
options: The small things, like spoons, bowls and things made of glass
mcqs.why: The small things, like spoons, bowls and things made of glass, are washed first. Only after that is soap applied and the other utensils scrubbed.

mcqs.q: What should you do after scrubbing all the other utensils?
options: Keep them in their place at once
Rinse all the scrubbed utensils one by one
mcqs.why: After scrubbing, you rinse all the scrubbed utensils one by one. Rinsing removes the soap and washing powder before drying them with a clean towel.

mcqs.q: What is the last step in washing dishes?
options: Keep them in their proper place
Take them to the washing area
mcqs.why: The last step is to keep them in their proper place. The work is complete only when the clean, dried utensils are put back where they belong.

mcqs.q: What is the first instruction for making tea?
options: Take a kettle and fill it with water
mcqs.why: Making tea begins with taking a kettle and filling it with water. Pouring, stirring and serving can only happen after the water has been heated and boiled.

mcqs.q: When do you add tea leaves when making tea?
options: After putting the kettle on the stove and heating the water, then boil
mcqs.why: You add tea leaves and boil the water after putting the kettle on the stove and heating the water. This order gives the tea its proper taste and colour.

mcqs.q: What should you do after adding milk and sugar to the tea?
options: Dry the cups with a towel
mcqs.why: After adding milk and sugar, you stir well. Stirring mixes everything properly before the tea is poured into cups and served to the guests.

mcqs.q: How is the tea served to the guests in the model instructions?
options: Put the cups on a tray with biscuits and serve the tea
Pour tea directly on the table
Give the kettle to the guests
mcqs.why: The cups are put on a tray with biscuits and then the tea is served to the guests. Serving on a tray with biscuits is the polite final step in the model.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a model rule students must follow in class?
mcqs.why: Raising your hand before speaking is a model class rule, along with wearing neat uniforms and coming on time. It keeps the class disciplined and orderly.

lessons.title: Writing: A Formal Email
lessons.notes_html:
Formal Email Format

  • To: the email address of the person or office.
  • Subject: a short, clear line stating the request.
  • Opening: Dear Sir,
  • Body: Begin with I am writing to request you to..., give the reason, and add a polite request such as I would appreciate it if you could / would...
  • Closing lines: Thank you for your kind consideration / cooperation. I look forward to hearing from you.
  • Ending: Yours sincerely / Yours faithfully, followed by name, class and school.

In all three model emails the writer is Ahmed Khan, Class VIII, Govt. High School, Jamshoro.

Email 1 — To the Traffic Department

  • To: traffic.department@example.com
  • Subject: Request to arrange a road safety awareness programme in our school.
  • Request: Arrange a road safety awareness programme in the school.
  • Details: The school has 500 students who should learn the traffic rules and the Green Cross Code. The department is asked to send a team of traffic police to teach the students.
  • Time requested: Next week, at a time suitable to the department.
  • Ending: Yours sincerely.

Email 2 — To the Nazim of the City/Town

  • To: nazim.city@example.com
  • Subject: Request to ensure knowledge of Traffic Safety rules before issuing driving licences.
  • Request: Ensure that people know the Traffic Safety rules before they are given a driving licence.
  • Reason: Many road accidents happen because people do not follow the traffic rules.
  • Suggestion: Make a short traffic safety test a part of the driving licence process, so every driver learns the rules first.
  • Ending: Yours faithfully.

Email 3 — To a News Channel

  • To: news.channel@example.com
  • Subject: Request to produce entertaining TV programmes on traffic safety.
  • Request: Produce some entertaining TV programmes on traffic safety.
  • Reason: Road accidents kill and injure many people because people do not follow the traffic rules.
  • Point: Appealing programmes on television can teach people the traffic rules, the Green Cross Code and safe road habits in an interesting way.
  • Ending: Yours faithfully.

mcqs.q: Who is the first formal email written to?
mcqs.why: The first email is written to the traffic department. Its purpose is to request a road safety awareness programme in the writer's school.

mcqs.q: What is the subject of the email to the traffic department?
options: Request to arrange a road safety awareness programme in our school
Request to build a new road
mcqs.why: Its subject is a request to arrange a road safety awareness programme in our school. The subject line clearly states the purpose of that email to the traffic department.

mcqs.q: How many students are there in Ahmed Khan's school, according to the first email?
mcqs.why: The email says the school has 500 students. This detail shows why a programme is needed, so that all 500 students can learn the traffic rules.

mcqs.q: What does the first email ask the traffic department to send?
options: A team of traffic police to teach the students
mcqs.why: It asks the department to send a team of traffic police to teach the students about road safety. The police team would teach the traffic rules and Green Cross Code.

mcqs.q: When does the first email request the programme to be arranged?
options: Next week, at a time suitable to the department
mcqs.why: The programme is requested for next week at a time suitable to the department. This polite wording leaves the exact time to the department's convenience.

mcqs.q: Who is the second formal email written to?
mcqs.why: The second email is written to the Nazim of the city or town. It asks him to ensure people know traffic safety rules before getting a driving licence.

mcqs.q: What suggestion is given in the email to the Nazim?
options: Make a short traffic safety test a part of the driving licence process
mcqs.why: The suggestion is to make a short traffic safety test a part of the driving licence process. In this way every driver would learn the rules before driving.

mcqs.q: Who is the third formal email written to?
mcqs.why: The third email is written to a news channel. It requests entertaining television programmes on traffic safety, because appealing programmes teach people in an interesting way.

mcqs.q: What can appealing TV programmes teach people, according to the third email?
options: The traffic rules, the Green Cross Code and safe road habits
How to drive without a licence
mcqs.why: Appealing programmes can teach the traffic rules, the Green Cross Code and safe road habits in an interesting way. That is the main argument of the email to the news channel.

mcqs.q: How does the writer sign all three model emails?
options: As a traffic policeman from Karachi
As Ahmed Khan, Class VIII, Govt. High School, Jamshoro
With no name or school given
mcqs.why: The writer is Ahmed Khan, Class VIII, Govt. High School, Jamshoro in all three emails. A formal email must end with the writer's full name, class and school.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Delivering a Presentation
lessons.notes_html:
About This Lesson

This is a thin lesson. It is built only from one model presentation outline on the topic The Importance of Reading. The outline shows how to organise a presentation into an introduction, main points and a conclusion.

Structure of a Presentation

PartWhat it contains
TitleThe Importance of Reading
IntroductionA. Greeting — B. Introductory statements — C. Purpose
Main pointsFirst main point with supporting points A and B; Second main point with supporting points A and B
ConclusionA. Closing statement — B. Summary — C. Suggestion

Model Outline — The Importance of Reading

  • Title: The Importance of Reading.
  • Introduction: A. Greeting: Good morning, everyone! B. Introductory statements: Reading is one of the most useful habits. C. Purpose: Today I will tell you why reading is important.
  • First main point: Reading increases knowledge. A. Books teach us new words and ideas. B. Reading helps us in all subjects.
  • Second main point: Reading improves our language. A. We learn correct English. B. We learn to write better.
  • Conclusion: A. In the end, reading is the key to learning. B. Summary: Reading increases knowledge and improves language. C. Suggestion: Everyone should read a book every week.

Key Points

  • Begin with a greeting, then give introductory statements, then state the purpose clearly.
  • Each main point needs supporting details labelled A and B.
  • End with a closing statement, a summary of both main points, and a practical suggestion.

mcqs.q: What is the topic of the model presentation outline?
mcqs.why: The model outline is on The Importance of Reading. The other two topics were choices in the task, but the outline actually prepared is about reading.

mcqs.q: What comes first in the introduction of the presentation?
mcqs.why: The introduction begins with a greeting — Good morning, everyone! Only after the greeting come the introductory statements and then the purpose of the presentation.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose statement in the model presentation?
options: Today I will visit three places
Today I will teach driving rules
Today I will tell you why reading is important
Today I will read a story aloud
mcqs.why: The purpose is: Today I will tell you why reading is important. Stating the purpose clearly in the introduction tells the audience what the presentation is about.

mcqs.q: What is the first main point of the presentation?
options: Reading is a waste of time
mcqs.why: The first main point is that reading increases knowledge. It is supported by two details: books teach new words and ideas, and reading helps in all subjects.

mcqs.q: Which supporting detail belongs to the first main point?
options: Books teach us new words and ideas
Reading is the key to learning
mcqs.why: Books teach us new words and ideas supports the first main point that reading increases knowledge. Learning to write better belongs to the second main point about language.

mcqs.q: How does reading help us in all subjects, according to the outline?
options: It is not mentioned at all
Reading helps us in all subjects
mcqs.why: The outline says reading helps us in all subjects as a supporting detail of the first main point. Knowledge gained from books is useful across the whole school course.

mcqs.q: What is the second main point of the presentation?
mcqs.why: The second main point is that reading improves our language. Its supporting details are that we learn correct English and we learn to write better.

mcqs.q: Which two things do we learn under the second main point?
options: Correct English and how to write better
mcqs.why: Under the second main point we learn correct English and we learn to write better. Both details show how reading improves our language skills.

mcqs.q: What does the conclusion say reading is?
mcqs.why: The conclusion says reading is the key to learning. This closing statement sums up the whole presentation before the summary and suggestion are given.

mcqs.q: What suggestion ends the model presentation?
options: Everyone should read a book every week
Read only one book in a year
mcqs.why: The suggestion is that everyone should read a book every week. Ending with a practical suggestion gives the audience a clear action to follow after the presentation.

lessons.title: Fun: Reading the News
lessons.notes_html:
Reading the News — What to Look For

For each news item we note: the name of the newspaper, the city from where it is reported, the date of reporting, who is mentioned, and what has been reported.

The Three News Items

NewspaperCityDateWho is mentionedWhat has been reported
Express NewsHyderabadDec 5At least five people, including two childrenThey were killed in a car-motorcycle collision during rain in Shahdadkot, in Sindh
DAWNRawalpindiJan 21Women of the twin citiesFor the first time, a women's transport service has been launched between Rawalpindi and Islamabad, starting Monday, February 4, 2014, with comfortable, safe and affordable facilities
The NationKarachiAug 5People who break certain traffic rulesKarachi Traffic police announced up to two years in prison for breaking traffic signals, disobeying one-way traffic signs, and travelling on the rooftop of buses and coaches

Key Points

  • News 1: A rain-time collision in Shahdadkot shows how dangerous roads become in bad weather.
  • News 2: The women's transport service between the twin cities Rawalpindi and Islamabad is a first-time facility.
  • News 3: Strict punishment — up to two years in prison — will apply to signal-breaking, one-way disobedience and rooftop travel.

mcqs.q: Which newspaper reported the Shahdadkot collision news?
mcqs.why: The collision news appeared in Express News, reported from Hyderabad on Dec 5. It tells of a car-motorcycle collision during rain in Shahdadkot, Sindh.

mcqs.q: How many people were killed in the Shahdadkot collision?
options: At least five people, including two children
mcqs.why: At least five people, including two children, were killed in the collision. The detail about the two children is an important part of who is mentioned in this news.

mcqs.q: Where did the collision in the first news item happen?
options: In Shahdadkot, in Sindh, during rain
mcqs.why: The collision happened in Shahdadkot, in Sindh, during rain. The news was reported from Hyderabad, but the accident itself took place in Shahdadkot.

mcqs.q: Which newspaper reported the women's transport service news?
mcqs.why: The women's transport service news appeared in DAWN, reported from Rawalpindi on Jan 21. It announces a first-time service for women between the twin cities.

mcqs.q: Between which two cities was the women's transport service launched?
mcqs.why: The service was launched between the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad. Women could now travel with comfortable, safe and affordable facilities.

mcqs.q: From when was the women's transport service to start?
mcqs.why: The service was to start from Monday, February 4, 2014, as reported on Jan 21. This exact starting date is a key detail of the DAWN news item.

mcqs.q: Which newspaper reported the Karachi traffic punishment news?
mcqs.why: The Karachi punishment news appeared in The Nation, reported from Karachi on Aug 5. It carries the traffic police announcement about prison for rule breakers.

mcqs.q: What punishment was announced for breaking certain traffic rules in Karachi?
options: Up to two years in prison
mcqs.why: The punishment announced is up to two years in prison. This strict punishment applies to people who break certain serious traffic rules in Karachi.

mcqs.q: Which action is punishable under the Karachi announcement?
mcqs.why: Breaking traffic signals is punishable, along with disobeying one-way signs and travelling on bus rooftops. Using footpaths and zebra crossings are safe actions, not offences.

mcqs.q: Travelling where is punishable under the Karachi announcement?
options: On the rooftop of buses and coaches
mcqs.why: Travelling on the rooftop of buses and coaches is punishable with up to two years in prison. Rooftop travel is dangerous, so the Karachi traffic police announced this strict rule.

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: Educational Exhibition
lessons.notes_html:
Text Summary

The text has 5 scenes. Students visit an educational exhibition and learn about different fields of study and work. In the order they visited them, the stalls were: the Agriculture stall, the Commerce stall, the Computer Sciences stall, the Medical and Engineering stall, and finally the Food stalls.

The students mentioned in the text are Juma, Anum, Rehmat, Majid, Sonia, Sudheer, Zainab and Fehmida.

Word Meanings

SceneWordMeaning
Iscoperange of choices
Iopportunitieschances
Imythstories that many people believe but are not true
Ireflectsshows
Ibreedingincreasing the number of animals through birth
IIcuriositywanting to know about everything
IIexposedshown what something is like
IIglobalat the world level
IIchallengespossible problems and issues
IIIvaluableuseful or important
IIIrapidlyquickly
IIIcommunicateget in touch with or talk to
IIIdramaticsudden and great
IIIanimatedpictures that move
IV and Vbackbonethe most important part
IV and Vcurrentlyat present
IV and Vamazingpleasurable
IV and Vconvincetry and make someone accept something
IV and Vdentalrelated to the teeth
IV and Voptimisma feeling that good things will happen

Branches of Agriculture

BranchDescription
Agronomysoil management and growing of crops
Horticulturecultivation of fruits, vegetables and flowers
Agricultural Engineeringknowledge of farm machines and equipment, and developing new systems and practices to address problems facing agriculture
Agricultural Economicsthe business end of farming
Animal Sciencebreeding and caring of animals for meat, milk and fur

Key Points

  • Agriculture is not only for boys. Girls can also take up agriculture, and universities teach both boys and girls. Five branches of agriculture are mentioned, not four.
  • Commerce is related to business: buying and selling, especially on a large scale. Rehmat wanted to set up business anywhere in the world, not only in Lahore.
  • Commerce education exposes students to the business world, prepares them for employment in commerce, finance and business fields and for establishing their own business, prepares them to meet global business challenges and compete in the international market, and can guide young graduates to become successful business people.
  • The students were excited about the computer stall because it had well-equipped, high-tech, new-generation computers and valuable information about a possible future profession in computers.
  • The world is progressing rapidly due to IT and almost all things are controlled with computers. One can communicate with anybody across the world. All official and unofficial work can be done through computers. Computers have brought a dramatic change in education, and they also give fun through games and 3D films.
  • Doctors serve humanity because they cure diseases and solve physical problems. Anum's father was a doctor, and Anum wanted to be an electronics engineer. The text says civil engineers are often paid more than electrical and electronics engineers.
  • Juma planned to be a civil engineer. Majid's father was a farmer. Sudheer wanted to be a male nurse. Rehmat had no plans as yet.

Fields of Study

  • Engineering fields: Mechanical, Electrical, Civil and Electronics engineering.
  • Medical fields: doctor, dentist and nurse, and Bachelors in Dental Surgery (BDS).

mcqs.q: How many scenes are there in the text about the educational exhibition?
mcqs.why: There are 5 scenes in the text, covering the agriculture, commerce, computer sciences, medical and engineering, and food stalls.

mcqs.q: Which stall did the students visit first?
mcqs.why: The Agriculture stall was visited first, before commerce, computer sciences, medical and engineering, and the food stalls.

mcqs.q: Which stalls did the students visit last?
mcqs.why: The Food stalls were visited last, after the students had been to all the other stalls in the exhibition.

mcqs.q: Which of these students is mentioned in the text?
mcqs.why: Sonia is one of the students mentioned in the text, along with Juma, Anum, Rehmat, Majid, Sudheer, Zainab and Fehmida.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'scope' mean in Scene I?
options: stories that many people believe but are not true
mcqs.why: Scope means range of choices, which is the meaning given for this word in the vocabulary of Scene I.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'curiosity' mean in Scene II?
mcqs.why: Curiosity means wanting to know about everything, which describes a strong wish to learn and find out more.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'animated' mean in Scene III?
mcqs.why: Animated means pictures that move, as in animated films and images shown on computers in Scene III.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'backbone' mean in Scenes IV and V?
options: try and make someone accept something
mcqs.why: Backbone means the most important part, the part that supports everything else, as used in Scenes IV and V.

mcqs.q: What is Agronomy?
options: soil management and growing of crops
cultivation of fruits, vegetables and flowers
breeding and caring of animals for meat, milk and fur
mcqs.why: Agronomy is soil management and growing of crops, one of the five branches of agriculture described in the text.

mcqs.q: What is Horticulture?
options: soil management and growing of crops
cultivation of fruits, vegetables and flowers
knowledge of farm machines and equipment
mcqs.why: Horticulture is the cultivation of fruits, vegetables and flowers, not the study of animals or farm machines.

mcqs.q: What is Agricultural Economics?
options: soil management and growing of crops
cultivation of fruits, vegetables and flowers
mcqs.why: Agricultural Economics is the business end of farming, dealing with the money and business side of agriculture.

mcqs.q: Which statement about Scene I is true?
options: Agriculture is a field only for boys
Only four branches of agriculture are mentioned
Agricultural engineering is related to the mechanical side of agriculture
mcqs.why: Agricultural engineering is related to the mechanical side of agriculture because it involves farm machines and equipment.

mcqs.q: What benefit does commerce education give students?
options: It teaches them only how to grow crops
It prepares them for employment in commerce, finance and business fields
It trains them to become doctors
It teaches them computer programming only
mcqs.why: Commerce education prepares students for employment in commerce, finance and business fields and for establishing their own business.

mcqs.q: Why were the students excited about the computer stall?
options: It had free food for all visitors
It had old computers for games only
It had well-equipped, high-tech, new-generation computers
It had farm machines on display
mcqs.why: The students were excited because the stall had well-equipped, high-tech, new-generation computers and valuable information about a future profession.

mcqs.q: What does BDS stand for in the medical fields of Scene IV?
mcqs.why: BDS stands for Bachelors in Dental Surgery, the medical field related to dentistry mentioned in Scene IV.

lessons.title: Speaking: Solving Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Text Summary

This speaking activity is done in a group of four. The group discusses a problem, identifies it clearly, and proposes solutions, following a sample dialogue pattern.

The Problem

Waheed asks Hamid why he seems cross today. Hamid explains that on the way to school he saw garbage lying everywhere in their street. Waheed says that is very sad and that their street should be clean. Hamid asks what they can do in this regard.

Proposed Solutions

lessons.title: Language Practice: Direct and Indirect Speech
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Points

When we report what someone said, we change direct speech into indirect speech. The reporting verb is usually in the past tense, so the tense of the reported sentence moves one step back.

  • can changes to could: Mujeeb said that he could not meet him after school that day.
  • is / am changes to was: Seema said that the food was very tasty there.
  • have been changes to had been: My parents said that they had been to Lahore several times.
  • forgot changes to had forgotten: Hania said that she had forgotten to call her mother that evening.
  • will changes to would: We said to our teacher that we would complete our work by the following week.
  • was sleeping changes to had been sleeping: I said that I had been sleeping when he came the previous night.
  • visited changes to had visited: Deeba said that they had visited their grandmother the previous summer.
  • have to changes to had to: My sister said that she had to finish her report by that night.
  • has seen / have seen changes to had seen: My brother said that he had already seen that movie.

Changes in Time and Place Words

Direct SpeechIndirect Speech
todaythat day
tomorrowthe next day / the following day
yesterdaythe previous day
last night / last week / last summerthe previous night / the previous week / the previous summer
next week / next year / next summerthe following week / the following year / the next summer
this evening / tonightthat evening / that night
herethere
thisthat

Changes in Pronouns

Pronouns change so that they agree with the reporter. For example, 'I cannot meet you' becomes 'he could not meet him', and 'We will complete our work' becomes 'they would complete their work' when reported by someone else.

Dialogue Example

Zeenat said that her sister was getting married the next day. Najma replied that she knew, and that her mother had told her the previous day. Zeenat said that she would wear a blue shalwar kameez and her mother would wear a yellow dress. Mahnoor said that that was why Zeenat had been absent the previous week, and Zeenat explained that she had had to go and invite people for the wedding.

mcqs.q: Mujeeb said to him, 'I cannot meet you after school today.' In indirect speech: Mujeeb said to him that he ___ him after school that day.
mcqs.why: Could not meet is correct because 'cannot' changes to 'could not' in indirect speech, and 'today' becomes 'that day'.

mcqs.q: Seema said, 'The food is very tasty here.' In indirect speech, 'is' and 'here' become:
mcqs.why: Was and there are correct because the present tense 'is' moves back to 'was', and 'here' changes to 'there' in reported speech.

mcqs.q: My parents said, 'We have been to Lahore several times.' In indirect speech, 'have been' becomes:
mcqs.why: Had been is correct because 'have been' moves one step back into the past perfect when the speech is reported.

mcqs.q: We said to the teacher, 'We will complete our work by next week.' In indirect speech, the work would be completed by:
mcqs.why: The following week is correct because 'will' changes to 'would' and 'next week' changes to 'the following week' in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: Manmohan said, 'I will visit Quetta next year.' In indirect speech, he said that he ___ Quetta the following year.
mcqs.why: Would visit is correct because 'will' changes to 'would' in indirect speech, and 'next year' becomes 'the following year'.

mcqs.q: All the mechanics said to us, 'We cannot fix your car.' In indirect speech, they said that they ___ our car.
mcqs.why: Could not fix is correct because 'cannot' changes to 'could not' when direct speech is reported in the past.

mcqs.q: My brother said to him, 'I've already seen this movie.' In indirect speech, 'I've already seen this movie' becomes 'he ___ already ___ ___ movie'.
mcqs.why: Had seen that is correct because 'have seen' becomes 'had seen' and 'this movie' becomes 'that movie' in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: Shah said, 'I don't like seafood.' In indirect speech: Shah said that he ___ seafood.
mcqs.why: Did not like is correct because the present simple 'don't like' moves back to the past simple in reported speech.

mcqs.q: I said, 'I was sleeping when you came last night.' In indirect speech, 'was sleeping' becomes:
mcqs.why: Had been sleeping is correct because the past continuous moves back to the past perfect continuous in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: Mariam said, 'I am planning to go to Turkey next summer.' In indirect speech, 'am planning' becomes:
mcqs.why: Was planning is correct because 'am planning' moves back to 'was planning', and 'next summer' becomes 'the next summer'.

mcqs.q: Deeba said, 'We visited our grandmother last summer.' In indirect speech, 'visited last summer' becomes:
mcqs.why: Had visited the previous summer is correct because the past simple moves back to the past perfect and 'last summer' becomes 'the previous summer'.

mcqs.q: The little girl said, 'I can't read Farsi.' In indirect speech: The little girl said that she ___ read Farsi.
mcqs.why: Could not is correct because 'can't' changes to 'could not' when the sentence is reported in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: My classmates said, 'We will come to the presentation tomorrow.' In indirect speech, 'tomorrow' becomes:
mcqs.why: The next day is correct because 'tomorrow' changes to 'the next day' and 'will come' changes to 'would come' in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: In the dialogue, Zeenat says her sister is getting married tomorrow. In indirect speech: Zeenat said that her sister ___ getting married the next day.
mcqs.why: Was is correct because 'is getting married' moves back to 'was getting married' and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'.

mcqs.q: Zeenat said, 'I had to go and invite people for the wedding.' In indirect speech, 'had to go' becomes:
mcqs.why: Had had to go is correct because 'had to' moves one step further back in reported speech, as shown in the dialogue conversion.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Adverbs of Manner
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Points

Adverbs of manner tell us how an action is done. Most adverbs of manner are made by adding -ly to an adjective.

  • Simple addition of -ly: glad → gladly, clever → cleverly, poor → poorly, sudden → suddenly, quick → quickly, cheap → cheaply, patient → patiently, real → really, proper → properly, comfortable → comfortably, peaceful → peacefully, hopeful → hopefully, thankful → thankfully, grateful → gratefully, careful → carefully.
  • Adjectives ending in -y change y to i before -ly: hungry → hungrily, lazy → lazily, noisy → noisily, easy → easily, heavy → heavily, angry → angrily.
  • Adjectives ending in -le drop the e and add -y: simple → simply, gentle → gently, possible → possibly.
  • Special spellings: true → truly, idle → idly.

Adverbs in Sentences

  • They were sitting comfortably and talking when they heard a loud noise.
  • The lights went off suddenly so the program had to end.
  • All the students were able to do the math paper easily.
  • We should all live peacefully with our neighbours.
  • The chairman left the meeting quickly because his wife was sick.
  • The people had not had food for two days so they ate hungrily.
  • The nurse lifted the baby gently and changed her clothes.
  • The office clerk gratefully took the money that his boss gave him.

Adverbs in Dialogue

Mariam left the room suddenly. She had done her work carefully but had made a big mistake. She could have easily explained to her friends. Hopefully she will be alright by lunch time. If her friends patiently wait, there will be no problem. People who always do their work properly get upset when things go wrong. Thankfully, her mood will get better by lunch time.

mcqs.q: What is the adverb form of 'glad'?
mcqs.why: Gladly is correct because most adverbs of manner are made by simply adding -ly to the adjective, so glad becomes gladly.

mcqs.q: What is the adverb form of 'hungry'?
mcqs.why: Hungrily is correct because an adjective ending in -y changes the y to i before adding -ly, so hungry becomes hungrily.

mcqs.q: What is the adverb form of 'true'?
mcqs.why: Truly is the correct adverb form of true; it is a special spelling in which the final e is dropped before -ly.

mcqs.q: What is the adverb form of 'gentle'?
mcqs.why: Gently is correct because an adjective ending in -le drops the e and adds -y, so gentle becomes gently.

mcqs.q: What is the adverb form of 'simple'?
mcqs.why: Simply is correct because simple ends in -le, so the e is dropped and -y is added to make the adverb.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: They were sitting ___ and talking when they heard a loud noise.
mcqs.why: Comfortably is correct because the people were sitting in a comfortable, relaxed way while talking, before the loud noise.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: The lights went off ___ so the program had to end.
mcqs.why: Suddenly is correct because the lights went off all at once and without warning, which is why the program had to end.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: The chairman left the meeting ___ because his wife was sick.
mcqs.why: Quickly is correct because the chairman had to leave in a hurry when he heard that his wife was sick.

mcqs.q: Complete the dialogue: '___ she will be alright by lunch time.'
mcqs.why: Hopefully is correct because Saba hopes that Mariam will be alright by lunch time after being upset about her mistake.

mcqs.q: Complete the dialogue: People who always do their work ___ get upset when things go wrong.
mcqs.why: Properly is correct because Saba means people who always do their work in the right way, so a mistake upsets them.

lessons.title: Writing: A Paragraph
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

A paragraph that shows the order of events uses sequence words: first, next, then, after that and finally.

Model Paragraph: Majid's Visit

The Government High School No. 2 Shikarpur organised an educational exhibition. All the children and their parents visited the stalls. Majid first visited the agriculture stall. He asked the agricultural expert about the scope of agriculture in Pakistan. Next, he visited the commerce stall. He asked the bank manager about the field of commerce and its benefits. Then, he visited the computer science stall. He learnt how computers help in work, communication, education and fun. After that, he visited the medical and engineering stall. He learnt about doctors, nurses and engineers. Finally, he went to the food stalls. He enjoyed delicious food and discussed his future plans. After visiting all the stalls he decided to become an agricultural engineer so that he could help his father in this field.

Narrative Paragraph

Today, when I reached near the school gate, I saw a big crowd. The school was decorated for the exhibition. I met my friends and we visited the stalls together. We learnt about many professions and enjoyed delicious food. It was a wonderful day.

Writing Tips

  • Begin with a clear opening sentence that names the event and who organised it.
  • Use one sequence word for each new step so the reader can follow the order easily.
  • End with a closing sentence that tells the result or feeling, such as Majid's decision or that it was a wonderful day.

mcqs.q: Which school organised the educational exhibition in the model paragraph?
options: The Government High School No. 2 Shikarpur
The Government High School No. 1 Karachi
mcqs.why: The Government High School No. 2 Shikarpur organised the exhibition, as stated in the opening sentence of the model paragraph.

mcqs.q: Which stall did Majid visit first?
mcqs.why: Majid first visited the agriculture stall, where he asked the agricultural expert about the scope of agriculture in Pakistan.

mcqs.q: Which stall did Majid visit next, after the agriculture stall?
mcqs.why: Next Majid visited the commerce stall, where he asked the bank manager about the field of commerce and its benefits.

mcqs.q: Which stall did Majid visit then, after the commerce stall?
mcqs.why: Then Majid visited the computer science stall, where he learnt how computers help in work, communication, education and fun.

mcqs.q: Which stall did Majid visit after that, following the computer science stall?
mcqs.why: After that Majid visited the medical and engineering stall, where he learnt about doctors, nurses and engineers.

mcqs.q: Where did Majid go finally, at the end of his visit?
mcqs.why: Finally Majid went to the food stalls, where he enjoyed delicious food and discussed his future plans.

mcqs.q: Whom did Majid ask about the scope of agriculture in Pakistan?
mcqs.why: Majid asked the agricultural expert about the scope of agriculture in Pakistan when he visited the agriculture stall first.

mcqs.q: Whom did Majid ask about the field of commerce and its benefits?
mcqs.why: Majid asked the bank manager about the field of commerce and its benefits when he visited the commerce stall.

mcqs.q: What did Majid decide to become after visiting all the stalls?
mcqs.why: Majid decided to become an agricultural engineer so that he could help his father in this field, as the paragraph concludes.

mcqs.q: In the narrative paragraph, what did the writer see near the school gate?
mcqs.why: The writer saw a big crowd near the school gate, because the school was decorated for the exhibition that day.

lessons.title: Fun: Fun with Nouns
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

The Fun poem plays with singular and plural nouns. Some plurals are regular, some change their form completely, and one noun stays exactly the same.

Singular and Plural Nouns from the Poem

SingularPlural
boxboxes
oxoxen
goosegeese
moosemoose
mousemice
househouses
manmen
panpans
footfeet
bootboots
toothteeth
boothbooths
thisthese
missmisses
thatthose
hathats
brotherbrothers (brethren)
mothermothers

Grammar Points

  • Regular plurals add -s or -es: box → boxes, house → houses, pan → pans, boot → boots, booth → booths, miss → misses, hat → hats, mother → mothers.
  • Irregular plurals change the word: goose → geese, mouse → mice, man → men, foot → feet, tooth → teeth.
  • Ox has the special plural oxen, and moose stays the same in the plural: moose → moose.
  • This changes to these, and that changes to those.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'box' in the Fun poem?
mcqs.why: Boxes is the plural of box, formed by adding -es, as listed from the Fun poem's singular and plural nouns.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'goose'?
mcqs.why: Geese is the irregular plural of goose; the whole word changes instead of simply adding -s or -es.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'mouse'?
mcqs.why: Mice is the irregular plural of mouse, one of the changed-form plurals played with in the Fun poem.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'moose'?
mcqs.why: Moose stays exactly the same in the plural, so one moose and many moose use the identical word.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'ox'?
mcqs.why: Oxen is the special plural of ox, an unusual form that does not follow the regular -s or -es rule.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'foot'?
mcqs.why: Feet is the irregular plural of foot; the vowel sound changes instead of an ending being added.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'tooth'?
mcqs.why: Teeth is the irregular plural of tooth, following the same changed-form pattern as foot and feet in the poem.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'this'?
mcqs.why: These is the plural form paired with this in the poem, just as those is the plural form paired with that.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'that'?
mcqs.why: Those is the plural form of that, matching the poem's pair this–these and that–those.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'man'?
mcqs.why: Men is the irregular plural of man; the word itself changes, like goose to geese and mouse to mice.

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: What Shaped Edhi's Life
lessons.notes_html:
Text Summary

Abdul Sattar Edhi was a great Pakistani humanitarian who served humanity regardless of religion, race and background. His mother had the most influence in shaping his life. She taught him love, kindness and service of humanity, and planted the seed of social welfare in him. That is why he chose to help people instead of earning money for himself.

Edhi was born in early 1928 in Bantva, Gujrat, British India. People gave him the title "Angel of Mercy". He started his humanitarian work in 1951 by establishing a very small dispensary in Mithadar, Karachi. His first ambulance service was called "Poor People's Van" and it was free. He died on July 8, 2016 in Karachi, Pakistan, and was the first common citizen of Pakistan in nearly seventy years to receive a state funeral.

Basic Information Form

ItemDetail
NameAbdul Sattar Edhi
Father's NameHaji Abdul Shakoor
Father's ProfessionDry fruit commission agent in Bombay
Grandfather's NameHaji Rehmatullah
Reasons for Grandfather's FameA simple, content and patient person who did not believe in surpluses and was known for resolving conflicts and settling disputes
Year of BirthEarly 1928
Place of BirthBantva, Gujrat, British India
Title given by peopleAngel of Mercy
Two services that made him famousAmbulance service and funeral service
Name of first ambulance servicePoor People's Van
Charges for first ambulance serviceFree — he did not charge; people who insisted dropped money in a box outside the dispensary
Date of deathJuly 8, 2016
Place of deathKarachi, Pakistan
Historical honourFirst common citizen of Pakistan in nearly seventy years to receive a state funeral

What His Mother Taught Him

  • Love and care, and kindness to the old, handicapped and mentally challenged.
  • To share food with poorer families.
  • To fear Allah and look after the mazlooms (the disadvantaged) and fulfil Huquq-ul-Ibaad, the rights of other human beings.
  • Not to waste time and to work to earn a living.
  • To control his desire for material things and overcome personal greed, and love for humanity.

Key Points

  • Edhi was mainly brought up by his mother because his father was mostly away from home. In Bantva, his friends called him Roti.
  • His father shaved his head because it is the most effective way to curb pride and prevent arrogance; it develops humility and truth.
  • His father was a truly optimistic person with high moral standards, simplicity and a positive attitude.
  • When Edhi's family migrated to Pakistan, they got into serious financial trouble.
  • As a boy, when mean kids made fun of the mentally challenged, Edhi would stop them.
  • More people came to know about his organisation because of the ambulance service. He often picked up bodies himself because family members refused to touch them.
  • His ambulance and funeral services grew all over Pakistan because no other organisation was doing this, not even the government.
  • He never spent time or money on himself because he had committed that nobody would get reason to challenge his integrity or lifestyle. He slept on a wooden bench in his dispensary so people could see how he was living.
  • He had only three pairs of clothes, one pair of plastic Chappal and one Jinnah Cap.
  • Today, the Edhi Foundation employs more than 7,000 people, both paid and voluntary workers.
  • Edhi's mission in life was to serve humanity, regardless of religion, race and background. He got a state funeral because of his great service to humanity.

Corrected Statements

  • Edhi started in 1951 with a small dispensary in Mithadar, Karachi — not in 1977 with an ambulance service.
  • His grandfather was simple, content and patient — not wealthy, rude and unkind.
  • His mother said fulfilling Huquq-ul-Ibaad was the first priority in Islam — not fulfilling one's own needs.
  • He did not charge for his ambulance service — not a lot of money.

Word Meanings

WordMeaning
