humbleLow
single-handedlyAll by himself
charitableHelping people who are poor or in need
voluntaryWork done by people who are not paid
networkA group of organizations working together
operateWork in a particular way
rehabilitation centresA place where people learn to live a useful life once again
drug-addictsPeople who regularly use harmful drugs
fondlyIn a loving way
recallsThink back about something
contentSatisfied
surplusesExtra things
disputesDisagreements
moral standardsLevels of right and wrong behaviour
optimisticAlways expecting good things to happen
conflictsFights
curbControl
arroganceProud behaviour
distractionSomething that takes away your attention
humilityConsidering oneself as someone very small
handicappedNot able to use a particular part of the body
mentally challengedNot able to use their mind properly
meanSelfish
appreciatedRecognise something good
fortunateLucky
confessedAdmit having done something wrong
disadvantagedNot having things that one needs for a proper living
prioritySomething that is more important than the other
ensuredMade sure
idlyDoing nothing
nurturedDeveloped
associateA person whom you work with or spend time with
transformationComplete change
insurmountableSomething that cannot be overcome
challengingDifficult
outlookThe way one looks at something
integrityHonesty
visionAbility to think about the future in an intelligent way
regardlessNot to give importance to something
state funeralA burial with honour given to the head of a state

mcqs.q: Who had the most influence in shaping Edhi's life?
mcqs.why: His mother had the most influence because she taught him love, kindness and service of humanity from childhood.

mcqs.q: Why did Edhi choose to help people instead of earning money for himself?
options: His father told him to do so
His mother taught him to be kind and charitable
He had a lot of money already
mcqs.why: His mother taught him to be kind and charitable and planted the seed of social welfare in him, so helping others became his aim.

mcqs.q: What does 'humanitarian work' mean?
options: Work that helps in making people's lives better
Work done only for earning profit
mcqs.why: Humanitarian work means work that helps in making people's lives better, which describes Edhi's service to poor and needy people.

mcqs.q: What was the name of Edhi's first ambulance service?
mcqs.why: Poor People's Van was the name of his first ambulance service, and it was free for people who needed it.

mcqs.q: What title did people give Edhi?
mcqs.why: People gave Edhi the title Angel of Mercy because of his kind ambulance, funeral and welfare services for humanity.

mcqs.q: When did Edhi start his humanitarian work, and how?
options: In 1977, by starting an ambulance service
In 1951, by establishing a very small dispensary in Mithadar, Karachi
In 2016, by starting the Edhi Foundation
mcqs.why: Edhi started his humanitarian work in 1951 by establishing a very small dispensary in Mithadar, Karachi, as the corrected statement shows.

mcqs.q: How many people does the Edhi Foundation employ today, according to the text?
options: More than 7,000 people, both paid and voluntary workers
mcqs.why: The Edhi Foundation employs more than 7,000 people, both paid and voluntary workers, across its large network of services.

mcqs.q: Why did Edhi's father shave his head?
options: To punish him for a mistake
To make him look different from friends
To curb pride and prevent arrogance, and develop humility and truth
mcqs.why: His father shaved his head because it is the most effective way to curb pride and prevent arrogance and to develop humility and truth.

mcqs.q: What does 'optimistic' mean, as used for Edhi's father?
options: Always expecting good things to happen
Not able to use the mind properly
mcqs.why: Optimistic means always expecting good things to happen, and Edhi's father was a truly optimistic person with a positive attitude.

mcqs.q: What did Edhi's mother say was the first priority in Islam?
options: Fulfilling Huquq-ul-Ibaad, the rights of other human beings
mcqs.why: His mother taught that fulfilling Huquq-ul-Ibaad, the rights of other human beings, was the first priority in Islam.

mcqs.q: What was Edhi's mission in life?
options: To serve humanity, regardless of religion, race and background
mcqs.why: Edhi's mission was to serve humanity regardless of religion, race and background, without giving importance to those differences.

mcqs.q: Why was Edhi given a state funeral?
options: Because he was head of a state
Because he asked for the honour
Because of his great service to humanity, as the first common citizen in nearly seventy years to receive one
mcqs.why: Because of his great service to humanity, Edhi received a state funeral and was the first common citizen in nearly seventy years to get this honour.

mcqs.q: What happened when Edhi's family migrated to Pakistan?
options: They became very rich at once
They got into serious financial trouble
mcqs.why: When Edhi's family migrated to Pakistan, they got into serious financial trouble, as the corrected statement in the lesson clearly states.

mcqs.q: How did Edhi live simply in his own life?
options: He had many clothes and dozens of shoes
He lived in a large house in Karachi
He had only three pairs of clothes, one pair of plastic Chappal and one Jinnah Cap, and slept on a wooden bench
He spent a lot of money on his family
mcqs.why: Edhi had only three pairs of clothes, one pair of plastic Chappal and one Jinnah Cap, and he slept on a wooden bench in his dispensary.

mcqs.q: What does 'rehabilitation centres' mean?
options: A place where people learn to live a useful life once again
A group of organizations working together
A burial with honour for a head of state
mcqs.why: Rehabilitation centres are places where people learn to live a useful life once again, such as centres helping drug-addicts recover.

lessons.title: Speaking: Expressing Needs and Requirements by Giving Reasons
lessons.notes_html:
Text Summary

In this speaking activity, two siblings talk about borrowing a bag. The brother expresses his need and gives a reason, promises to take care of the bag, and thanks his sister. The sister first refuses for a reason, then agrees with a condition.

Model Dialogue

  • Brother: Can I borrow your bag today?
  • Sister: No, I won't give you my bag. It's a gift from my friend and you will tear it.
  • Brother: I promise you I'll take good care of it. I need it because I have to carry my books to school and my bag is torn.
  • Sister: Ok, you can take it but take good care of it and return it in the evening.
  • Brother: Thank you. I'll return it safely in the evening.

Key Points

  • To express a need, say what you need and give a reason with "because": "I need it because..."
  • Give a reason when you refuse: the bag is a gift from a friend and it may be torn.
  • Make a promise to reassure: "I promise you I'll take good care of it."
  • Agree with a condition using "but": you can take it, but return it in the evening.
  • End politely with thanks and a clear promise to return the thing safely.

mcqs.q: In the dialogue, what does the brother ask to borrow?
mcqs.why: The brother asks to borrow his sister's bag, which is the need around which the whole speaking dialogue is built.

mcqs.q: Why does the sister first refuse to give the bag?
options: She needs the bag herself that day
It is a gift from her friend and she fears he will tear it
She wants money for the bag
mcqs.why: The sister refuses because the bag is a gift from her friend and she says he will tear it, so she wants to protect it.

mcqs.q: What reason does the brother give for needing the bag?
options: He wants to carry his books to school and his own bag is torn
He wants to give it to a friend
He has no books to carry
mcqs.why: The brother needs the bag because he has to carry his books to school and his own bag is torn, which is his stated reason.

mcqs.q: What promise does the brother make?
options: He will buy a new bag
He will return it next week
He will take good care of it
mcqs.why: The brother promises he will take good care of the bag, and later promises to return it safely in the evening.

mcqs.q: Which word does the brother use to give his reason?
mcqs.why: The brother uses because to give his reason when he says he needs the bag because his own bag is torn.

mcqs.q: With what condition does the sister finally agree?
options: He must pay for the bag
He must take good care of it and return it in the evening
He must ask her friend first
He must carry her books too
mcqs.why: The sister agrees on the condition that he takes good care of the bag and returns it in the evening, as the model completion shows.

mcqs.q: How does the brother end the dialogue?
options: By thanking her and promising to return it safely in the evening
mcqs.why: The brother ends politely by thanking his sister and promising to return the bag safely in the evening.

mcqs.q: Why is giving a reason useful when expressing a need?
options: It helps the other person understand why you need something
It makes the request longer for no purpose
It means you never have to return things
mcqs.why: Giving a reason helps the other person understand why you need something, which is the main speaking skill practised in this dialogue.

mcqs.q: What is the sister worried will happen to the bag?
options: It will be lost at school
It will get wet in rain
mcqs.why: The sister is worried he will tear the bag, which is why she first refuses and later asks him to take good care of it.

mcqs.q: Which sentence expresses a need with a reason?
options: Can I borrow your bag today?
I need it because I have to carry my books to school and my bag is torn.
Thank you, I will return it.
mcqs.why: The sentence with because expresses the need and its reason together: the books must be carried and the brother's own bag is torn.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Tag Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Points

A question tag is a short question added at the end of a statement to confirm something or ask for agreement, for example: "The train is late today, isn't it?"

  • If the statement is positive, the tag is negative: "The children are really enjoying themselves, aren't they?"
  • If the statement is negative, the tag is positive: "My bag isn't under the table, is it?" and "We haven't paid our electric bill, have we?"
  • Use the same helping verb in the tag: is, are, has, have, can, will, should, do and does.
  • For a simple present statement without a helping verb, use don't / doesn't: "My mother cleans the house every day, doesn't she?"
  • For a simple past statement, use didn't: "They finished their work on time, didn't they?"
  • Change the subject to the right pronoun in the tag: he, she, it, they, we, you or I.

Key Points

StatementTag Question
You can't open this lock with your keycan you?
The teacher won't take the test todaywill he?
The team has practised a lot todayhaven't they?
The students should obey the school rulesshouldn't they?
Our football team can win this matchcan't it?
I will get good grades in my examswon't I?
We are going on a field trip this Saturdayaren't we?
Mr. Mirza won't comewill he?
Last time they did and we had a great timedidn't we?
We can always catch up on our sleepcan't we?

Remember: a negative statement takes a positive tag, and a positive statement takes a negative tag.

mcqs.q: Add the correct tag: 'My bag isn't under the table, ___?'
mcqs.why: The statement is negative with isn't, so the tag is positive and uses the same verb: is it completes the sentence correctly.

mcqs.q: Add the correct tag: 'The children are really enjoying themselves, ___?'
mcqs.why: The positive statement uses are with the children, so the negative tag is aren't they, matching verb and pronoun.

mcqs.q: Add the correct tag: 'The old man looks very tired, ___?'
mcqs.why: Looks is a simple present verb without a helping verb, so the tag uses doesn't he for the old man.

mcqs.q: Add the correct tag: 'You can't open this lock with your key, ___?'
mcqs.why: Can't makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive and keeps the same modal verb: can you is correct.

mcqs.q: Add the correct tag: 'The team has practised a lot today, ___?'
mcqs.why: The book's tag for the team statement is haven't they, following the has practised form given in the exercise answers.

mcqs.q: Add the correct tag: 'The teacher won't take the test today, ___?'
mcqs.why: Won't makes the statement negative, so the positive tag will he is needed with the same modal verb will.

mcqs.q: Add the correct tag: 'We haven't paid our electric bill, ___?'
mcqs.why: Haven't makes the statement negative, so the tag is the positive have we, using the same helping verb have.

mcqs.q: Add the correct tag: 'My mother cleans the house every day, ___?'
mcqs.why: Cleans is simple present with no helping verb, and the subject is my mother, so the negative tag is doesn't she.

mcqs.q: What is the basic rule for question tags?
options: A positive statement takes a negative tag, and a negative statement takes a positive tag
mcqs.why: The basic rule is that a positive statement takes a negative tag and a negative statement takes a positive tag, as all the examples show.

mcqs.q: Add the correct tag: 'They finished their work on time, ___?'
mcqs.why: Finished is simple past with no helping verb, so the tag uses didn't they to match the past tense and subject.

mcqs.q: Add the correct tag: 'The students should obey the school rules, ___?'
mcqs.why: The positive statement uses should, so the negative tag keeps that modal verb: shouldn't they is the correct form.

mcqs.q: Add the correct tag: 'I will get good grades in my exams, ___?'
mcqs.why: The positive statement uses will with I, so the negative tag is won't I, matching the verb and the subject pronoun.

mcqs.q: Add the correct tag: 'We are going on a field trip this Saturday, ___?'
mcqs.why: The dialogue uses aren't we after the positive are statement about the field trip, confirming the plan with Hamza and Zaman.

mcqs.q: Add the correct tag: 'Your tea is getting cold, ___?'
mcqs.why: Tea is treated as it and the verb is is, so the negative tag for the positive statement is isn't it.

mcqs.q: Add the correct tag: 'I don't know how to drive a car, ___?'
mcqs.why: Don't makes the statement negative, so the positive tag is do I, using the same verb do and the subject I.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Linking Words
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Points

Linking words join two sentences or ideas. In this unit we use and, but and because.

  • and joins two similar or adding ideas: "Our house is big and it has a nice view of the river."
  • but joins two contrasting ideas: "The colour of this dress is nice, but I like the colour of the dress that you bought."
  • because gives a reason: "My sister wants to go to university because she wants to become an engineer."

Key Points

Joined SentenceLinking Word and Reason
We can reach Gilgit faster by air, but travelling by road is much fun.but — contrast
Growing vegetables at home is good because we can have fresh vegetables to eat.because — reason
People give money to those who need it and they also give voluntary time.and — addition
We should protect ourselves from mosquitoes because mosquito bites can cause malaria.because — reason
Our school gets over at twelve, but I reach home at two o'clock.but — contrast
I decided to have an early dinner because I wanted to sleep early.because — reason
They wanted to return the bag to the shopkeeper but they forgot the bag at home.but — contrast
She bought a new dress for Eid and she also bought a new pair of sandals.and — addition
His parents took his baby sister to the doctor because she had high fever.because — reason
The player tried his best to catch the ball but the ball went to the boundary for four runs.but — contrast

mcqs.q: Join correctly: 'Our house is big. It has a nice view of the river.'
options: Our house is big but it has a nice view of the river
Our house is big because it has a nice view of the river
Our house is big and it has a nice view of the river
Our house is big or it has a nice view of the river
mcqs.why: And joins two adding ideas here, because having a nice view adds to the house being big rather than contrasting with it.

mcqs.q: Join correctly: 'My sister wants to go to university. She wants to become an engineer.'
options: My sister wants to go to university because she wants to become an engineer
My sister wants to go to university but she wants to become an engineer
My sister wants to go to university and she wants to become an engineer yesterday
My sister wants to go to university or she wants to become an engineer
mcqs.why: Because gives the reason for going to university, namely that she wants to become an engineer, so it links cause and aim.

mcqs.q: Which linking word shows contrast?
mcqs.why: But shows contrast between two different ideas, as in liking one dress colour but preferring the colour of another dress.

mcqs.q: Join correctly: 'We should protect ourselves from mosquitoes. Mosquito bites can cause malaria.'
options: We should protect ourselves from mosquitoes and mosquito bites can cause malaria only
We should protect ourselves from mosquitoes but mosquito bites can cause malaria today
We should protect ourselves from mosquitoes or mosquito bites can cause malaria
We should protect ourselves from mosquitoes because mosquito bites can cause malaria
mcqs.why: Because gives the reason for protection: mosquito bites can cause malaria, so the reason word correctly joins the pair.

mcqs.q: Join correctly: 'She bought a new dress for Eid. She also bought a new pair of sandals.'
options: She bought a new dress for Eid but she also bought sandals
She bought a new dress for Eid and she also bought a new pair of sandals
She bought a new dress for Eid because she also bought sandals
She bought a new dress for Eid or sandals
mcqs.why: And joins the two adding purchases, a new dress for Eid and also a new pair of sandals, without any contrast or reason.

mcqs.q: Join correctly: 'They left home early to catch the train. They missed their train due to a traffic jam.'
options: They left home early to catch the train and they missed it happily
They left home early to catch the train because they missed it
They left home early to catch the train but they missed their train due to a traffic jam
They left home early to catch the train or they missed it
mcqs.why: But shows the contrast between leaving early to catch the train and still missing it due to a traffic jam.

mcqs.q: Why did his parents take his baby sister to the doctor, in the joined sentence?
options: And she had high fever only
mcqs.why: His parents took his baby sister to the doctor because she had high fever, so because correctly introduces the reason.

mcqs.q: Join correctly: 'The food in this restaurant is good. The food in the restaurant across the street is better.'
options: The food in this restaurant is good because the other food is better
The food in this restaurant is good and the other food is worse
The food in this restaurant is good or the other food is better
The food in this restaurant is good, but the food in the restaurant across the street is better
mcqs.why: But contrasts the good food in this restaurant with the better food across the street, which is the relationship between the ideas.

mcqs.q: Which linking word gives a reason?
mcqs.why: Because gives a reason, as when neighbours sold their old house because they wanted to buy a new one.

mcqs.q: Complete with a suitable idea: 'He decided to wash the dishes because ___.'
mcqs.why: The model completion says he decided to wash the dishes because they were dirty, giving a clear reason for the action.

lessons.title: Writing: A Paragraph
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Points

An "If..." sentence shows an action and its effect. The part after "If" gives the action or condition, and the second part gives the result.

ActionEffect
If we don't wash our hands before eatingwe will fall sick
If students do not follow the school rulesthere will be disorder in the school / they will be punished
If we keep our village/city cleanwe will stay healthy and our surroundings will look beautiful
If students do not study properlythey will fail in the exams
If people break the traffic rulesthere will be accidents
If children do not obey their parentsthey will get into trouble
If we do protect ourselves from mosquitoeswe will not get malaria
If we do drink clean waterwe will stay healthy
If people work honestlythey will succeed and the country will progress

Writing a Paragraph

First make a mind map on one topic, then write a paragraph from it. The three topics were: Population growth and its impact; Misuse of natural resources and its impact on future generations; Pollution and its impact on people's health.

Model Paragraph: Pollution and Its Impact on People's Health

Pollution is very harmful for our health. Smoke from vehicles and factories pollutes the air and causes breathing problems. Dirty water causes diseases like cholera. Noise pollution disturbs our sleep and makes us tired. If we plant trees, keep our surroundings clean and do not burn garbage, we can reduce pollution and stay healthy.

Key Points

  • Air pollution from vehicle and factory smoke causes breathing problems.
  • Dirty water causes diseases like cholera.
  • Noise pollution disturbs sleep and makes us tired.
  • We can reduce pollution by planting trees, keeping surroundings clean and not burning garbage.

mcqs.q: What is the effect in: 'If we don't wash our hands before eating, ___'?
mcqs.why: The given effect is we will fall sick, showing that not washing hands before eating leads to illness.

mcqs.q: What happens if students do not study properly?
options: They will fail in the exams
mcqs.why: If students do not study properly, they will fail in the exams, which is the direct effect stated in the exercise.

mcqs.q: What is the effect of keeping our village/city clean?
options: We will stay healthy and our surroundings will look beautiful
mcqs.why: Keeping the village or city clean means we will stay healthy and our surroundings will look beautiful, a positive effect.

mcqs.q: What happens if people break the traffic rules?
mcqs.why: If people break the traffic rules, there will be accidents, so following traffic rules protects people on the road.

mcqs.q: How can we avoid malaria, according to the If sentences?
mcqs.why: If we do protect ourselves from mosquitoes, we will not get malaria, so protection from mosquitoes is the way to avoid it.

mcqs.q: In the model paragraph, what does smoke from vehicles and factories cause?
mcqs.why: Smoke from vehicles and factories pollutes the air and causes breathing problems, as the model paragraph on pollution states.

mcqs.q: Which disease is linked to dirty water in the model paragraph?
mcqs.why: Dirty water causes diseases like cholera in the model paragraph, while smoke is linked to breathing problems and noise to tiredness.

mcqs.q: What does noise pollution do, according to the paragraph?
options: Disturbs our sleep and makes us tired
mcqs.why: Noise pollution disturbs our sleep and makes us tired, which is one of the three harms described in the model paragraph.

mcqs.q: Which is one way to reduce pollution, from the paragraph?
options: Plant trees and keep our surroundings clean
mcqs.why: Planting trees, keeping surroundings clean and not burning garbage can reduce pollution and help us stay healthy.

mcqs.q: What is the first step before writing the paragraph in this task?
options: Copy the paragraph from a friend
Learn all the If sentences by heart
Make a mind map on one of the given topics
mcqs.why: The task first asks learners to make a mind map on one topic and then write a paragraph on it, so planning comes before writing.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Weekly Planner
lessons.notes_html:
Text Summary

Plan your week to be an effective student. Make a weekly planner. Ali fills his weekly planner in order to be more organized and disciplined.

Ali's Weekly Planner

Time / Part of DayActivity
5:00–6:00 a.m.Wakes up early
7:00 a.m.Breakfast
8:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.School
After schoolGo home / school club, practice, study, sports/music, chores
6:00 p.m.Dinner
EveningStudy or free time
8:00 p.m.Free time

How to Make Your Own Weekly Schedule

  • Determine when you are in class, playing, doing chores, watching television, etc.
  • Plan the best time each day for study and homework and write it on the planner.
  • Allow at least 2–3 hours per day for study and homework.
  • Look at all the free time you still have.
  • Do a lot of studying during the week and free up your weekends to have fun with your friends and family.

Key Points

  • A weekly planner helps a student be more organized and disciplined.
  • Study and homework need a fixed, planned time every day — at least 2–3 hours.

mcqs.q: Why does Ali fill his weekly planner?
options: To be more organized and disciplined
mcqs.why: Ali fills his weekly planner in order to be more organized and disciplined, which is the purpose of planning the week.

mcqs.q: At what time does Ali have breakfast?
mcqs.why: Ali has breakfast at 7:00 a.m., after waking up early between 5:00 and 6:00 a.m. and before school starts.

mcqs.q: What are Ali's school hours in the planner?
mcqs.why: School in Ali's planner runs from 8:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., followed by home, club, practice, study, sports or music and chores.

mcqs.q: How much time should you allow each day for study and homework?
mcqs.why: The planner advice says to allow at least 2–3 hours per day for study and homework, planned at the best time each day.

mcqs.q: What is the first step in making your own weekly schedule?
options: Determine when you are in class, playing, doing chores, watching television, etc.
Study for three hours at once
mcqs.why: The first step is to determine when you are in class, playing, doing chores, watching television and so on, before fixing study time.

mcqs.q: Why should you do a lot of studying during the week?
options: To free up your weekends to have fun with friends and family
mcqs.why: Doing a lot of studying during the week frees up weekends to have fun with friends and family, as the study skills section advises.

mcqs.q: At what time does Ali have dinner?
mcqs.why: Ali has dinner at 6:00 p.m. in his planner, after afternoon activities and chores and before evening study or free time.

mcqs.q: What does a weekly planner help a student become?
options: An effective, organized and disciplined student
mcqs.why: Planning your week helps you be an effective student, and Ali uses his planner to be more organized and disciplined.

mcqs.q: When does Ali wake up in his planner?
mcqs.why: Ali wakes up early, between 5:00 and 6:00 a.m., which is the first entry shown in his weekly planner.

mcqs.q: What should you write on the planner for study and homework?
options: The best time each day for study and homework
mcqs.why: You should plan the best time each day for study and homework and write it on the planner, so study gets a fixed daily place.

lessons.title: Fun: Creating a Personal Flag
lessons.notes_html:
Text Summary

Take a sheet of paper and some colour pencils, paint or pictures. On the sheet of paper, draw a personal flag that describes you.

Key Points

  • The flag must have 4–6 sections.
  • In each section there should be a drawing or symbol that shows something about you.
  • For example, one section can contain a picture of your favourite food; another section could show your hobby, favourite animal, favourite game and so on.
  • You can draw, colour, paint or stick small pictures on the flag.
  • Choose the background colour that you want.
  • You have 20 minutes to draw your personal flag.
  • When you finish, show your flag to your classmates and explain to them what you have drawn and why.

mcqs.q: What should a personal flag describe?
mcqs.why: A personal flag should describe you, with each section showing something about you through a drawing or symbol.

mcqs.q: How many sections must the personal flag have?
mcqs.why: The flag must have 4–6 sections, and each section should contain a drawing or symbol about you.

mcqs.q: What should each section of the flag contain?
options: A drawing or symbol that shows something about you
A copy of a national flag
mcqs.why: Each section should have a drawing or symbol that shows something about you, such as a favourite food, hobby, animal or game.

mcqs.q: How much time do you have to draw your personal flag?
mcqs.why: You have 20 minutes to draw your personal flag, so the activity must be completed within that short class time.

mcqs.q: What can you do to make the flag?
options: Draw, colour, paint or stick small pictures on the flag
mcqs.why: You can draw, colour, paint or stick small pictures on the flag, using colour pencils, paint or pictures as you choose.

mcqs.q: Who chooses the background colour of the flag?
options: You — choose the background colour that you want
mcqs.why: You choose the background colour that you want, because the flag is personal and describes your own choices.

mcqs.q: What should you do when you finish the flag?
options: Keep it secret and say nothing
Show it to your classmates and explain what you have drawn and why
mcqs.why: When you finish, show your flag to your classmates and explain to them what you have drawn and why you chose it.

mcqs.q: Which is a suitable example for one section of the flag?
options: A picture of your favourite food
mcqs.why: One section can contain a picture of your favourite food, and other sections can show a hobby, favourite animal or favourite game.

mcqs.q: What do you need to start the activity?
options: A sheet of paper and some colour pencils, paint or pictures
mcqs.why: You need a sheet of paper and some colour pencils, paint or pictures to draw your personal flag on the sheet.

mcqs.q: Why does each section use a symbol?
mcqs.why: Each section uses a drawing or symbol to show something about you, so classmates can learn about your likes and hobbies.

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: Sportsmanship
lessons.notes_html:
Story Summary

Rajoo was a great cricketer who played for the Ranikot district. After his team won in Australia, the team received a resounding welcome on its return. Success went to Rajoo's head. He became rude and arrogant, and both national and international players did not like his attitude. Because of his rude attitude, the cricket board decided to ban him from the team.

When Rajoo came to Ranikot, the town people invited him to the town hall to honour their hero and hear the stories of his victories. They listened to him in awe. His friend Nabeel was very excited to meet him, but he was shocked because Rajoo refused to recognise him.

Nabeel gave Rajoo a scrapbook full of stories of sportsmanship. Reading it changed Rajoo. He realised that greatness lies in sportsmanship, not in achievements alone. At a press conference he apologised publicly for his rude behaviour. The cricket board took him back because he was a great player, and when he went back to his team he took the scrapbook with him.

Main Idea

The main idea of the text is: It is never too late to change. Rajoo realised his mistake, apologised and was welcomed back.

Word Meanings

  • broke into applause: clapped very loudly
  • went to his head: made him very proud
  • rude: not showing respect
  • arrogant: behaving in a proud manner
  • irritating: something that makes people a little angry
  • counselled: advised
  • to no avail: it did not have any effect
  • resounding: very great
  • well-suited: well dressed
  • awe: feeling of respect
  • renowned: famous, well-known
  • chatting: talking in a friendly way
  • pranks: tricks played on someone as a joke
  • scrap-book: a book in which one sticks pictures or newspaper articles
  • intolerable: unacceptable
  • sportsmanship: fair, generous and polite behaviour

The Five Scrapbook Articles

ArticleStorySportsmanship Shown
Article 1Mark Taylor and the record of 375 runs held by Brian Lara; Don Bradman had scored 334 runs in 1930Chose team interest over self interest - he wanted his team to win the match against Pakistan
Article 2Daniel Vettori, 2012, New Zealand against Zimbabwe; he collided with Malcolm Waller and Regis Chakabva got outAccepted fault in the other player's failure - he withdrew the umpire's decision
Article 3Sri Lanka against Australia; Andrew Symonds was actually not out but the umpire gave a wrong decision because the Sri Lankans shouted loudlySurprised the player by calling him back - Marvan Atapattu called Symonds back from the pavilion
Article 4At Lahore, the visiting team faced a strong Pakistani bowling attack by Waqar Younis and Aaqib JavedOne captain gave another captain a second chance - the Pakistan captain called back the visiting captain, but Waqar got him out on the next ball
Article 51987 World Cup in Lahore; Pakistan needed two runs with only one ball leftSaved the opposite team's player and lost the match - Courtney Walsh did not run out the non-striker, Abdul Qadir scored the runs and Pakistan won

Key Points

  • People did not like Rajoo because success went to his head and he became rude and arrogant.
  • Nabeel had counselled and helped Rajoo, so Rajoo was later happy to see him in the playground.
  • The scrapbook contained five articles showing fair, generous and polite behaviour in cricket.
  • Reading the scrapbook brought the good change in Rajoo.

mcqs.q: What is the main idea of the text about Rajoo?
options: It is never too late to change
All cricketers are liked by the people
A great Pakistani cricketer is born
mcqs.why: The correct idea is 'It is never too late to change' because Rajoo realised his mistake, apologised for his rude behaviour and was welcomed back into the team.

mcqs.q: Why did people not like Rajoo even though he was a great player?
options: He played for the Ranikot district
He won a match in Australia
Success went to his head and he became rude and arrogant
He read a scrapbook in Ranikot
mcqs.why: Success went to his head is correct because the text says Rajoo became very rude and arrogant, and his attitude annoyed both local and international players.

mcqs.q: What does 'sportsmanship' mean in the unit?
options: Playing only to win a match
mcqs.why: Sportsmanship means fair, generous and polite behaviour. This is the quality shown in all five scrapbook stories and the quality Rajoo finally learns.

mcqs.q: Why was Nabeel shocked by Rajoo's behaviour?
options: Rajoo invited him to the town hall
Rajoo apologised at a press conference
mcqs.why: Nabeel was shocked because Rajoo refused to recognise him. Nabeel was Rajoo's friend who had counselled and helped him in the past.

mcqs.q: What did the people of Ranikot do when Rajoo came back after the Australia tour?
options: They banned him from the team
They invited him to the town hall to hear stories of his victories
They asked him to leave Ranikot
mcqs.why: The people invited Rajoo to the town hall to honour their hero and hear the stories of his victories, and they listened to his stories in awe.

mcqs.q: What was inside the scrapbook that Nabeel gave to Rajoo?
options: Scores of matches played in Australia
Wonderful stories of players and their sportsmanship
mcqs.why: The scrapbook was full of wonderful stories of players and their sportsmanship, with five articles showing fair, generous and polite behaviour in cricket.

mcqs.q: In Article 1, whose world record of 375 runs is mentioned?
mcqs.why: The world record of 375 runs was held by Brian Lara. Article 1 also notes that Don Bradman had scored 334 runs in 1930.

mcqs.q: What did Mark Taylor do in Article 1?
options: He chose team interest over self interest
He called back a player from the pavilion
He did not run out the non-striker
mcqs.why: Mark Taylor chose team interest over self interest because he wanted his team to win the match against Pakistan instead of seeking personal glory.

mcqs.q: In Article 2, what did Daniel Vettori do after his collision caused a player to get out?
options: He left the match against Zimbabwe

mcqs.q: In Article 3, who called Andrew Symonds back?

options: Symonds had left the pavilion early

mcqs.q: In Article 4 at Lahore, which two great Pakistani bowlers are named?
mcqs.why: Waqar Younis and Aaqib Javed are named as Pakistan's great bowlers in Article 4, where the visiting team faced a strong Pakistani bowling attack at Lahore.

mcqs.q: In Article 5, what great sportsmanship did Courtney Walsh show?
options: He withdrew an appeal against Zimbabwe
He did not run out the non-striker and Pakistan won
He gave his own wicket to Pakistan
He called the visiting captain back

lessons.title: Speaking: Negotiating and Reaching Consensus
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Negotiating?

In this lesson three friends talk together to decide about a class picnic. Negotiating means discussing different views, listening to problems and finally reaching consensus, which means an agreement that everyone accepts.

The Model Dialogue

  • Student A suggests: "I think we should go to Keenjhar Lake for the class picnic."
  • Student B agrees but raises a problem: it is far away and the bus will cost a lot of money.
  • Student C replies that a picnic is fun only when we go to a nice place.
  • Student A suggests money: "We can go if we all pay Rs. 200 each."
  • Student B points out that it is not only the bus fare; money will also be needed for food.
  • Student C says a picnic is fun only when we have good food too.
  • Student A adds a caution: we should also be careful not to spend too much money.

Reaching Consensus

Student B suggests making a list of students who want to go, so the total cost can be decided. Student C agrees: once we know how many students are going, we can decide the food and the money. At the end all three say together: "Agreed!"

Key Points

  • Three questions are negotiated: where to go, who will go, and how much money to charge.
  • Place decided in discussion: Keenjhar Lake.
  • Amount first suggested: Rs. 200 each, plus money needed for food.
  • Final step before deciding cost: make a list of students who want to go.

mcqs.q: Where does Student A suggest going for the class picnic?
mcqs.why: Keenjhar Lake is correct because Student A opens the dialogue by saying the class should go to Keenjhar Lake for the class picnic.

mcqs.q: What problem does Student B raise about Keenjhar Lake?
options: The food there is not good
It is far away and the bus will cost a lot of money
Too few students want to go there
It is not a nice place for a picnic
mcqs.why: Student B says Keenjhar Lake is far away and the bus will cost a lot of money, which is the cost problem the friends must negotiate.

mcqs.q: How much money does Student A first suggest each student should pay?
mcqs.why: Rs. 200 each is correct because Student A says the class can go to Keenjhar Lake if everyone pays Rs. 200 each for the picnic.

mcqs.q: Besides the bus fare, what else does Student B say money will be needed for?
mcqs.why: Food is correct because Student B reminds the friends that it is not only the bus fare and that they will also need money for food.

mcqs.q: What does Student C say makes a picnic fun about the place?
options: A picnic is fun only when we go to a nice place
A picnic is fun only when it costs little money
A picnic is fun only near the school
A picnic is fun only without a bus
mcqs.why: Student C says a picnic is fun only when we go to a nice place, so C supports going to Keenjhar Lake despite the distance and bus cost.

mcqs.q: What does Student C say about food for the picnic?
options: Food money is not needed at all
A picnic is fun only when we have good food too
Students should bring food money later
Good food makes the bus cheaper
mcqs.why: Student C says a picnic is fun only when we have good food too, supporting Student B's point that food money must be added to the cost.

mcqs.q: What caution does Student A add about spending?
options: Spend as much money as possible
Be careful not to spend too much money
Do not make a list of students
mcqs.why: Student A says the friends should be careful not to spend too much money, balancing the nice place and good food against the total cost.

mcqs.q: What does Student B suggest making before deciding the total cost?
options: A list of food items only
A list of students who want to go
mcqs.why: A list of students who want to go is correct because Student B says that once the list is made, the friends can decide the total cost.

mcqs.q: According to Student C, what can be decided once the number of students is known?
options: The winner of the picnic game
mcqs.why: The food and the money can be decided once the number is known, because Student C says knowing how many students are going helps decide both things.

mcqs.q: How does the dialogue end when consensus is reached?
options: They decide to cancel the picnic
mcqs.why: All say 'Agreed!' together is correct because the dialogue ends with full consensus after the place, list, food and money points are settled.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Comparative Adjectives — The... The...
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Points

The pattern The + comparative adjective ... , the + comparative adjective ... shows that one change causes another change. Example: The faster the train, the sooner we will reach.

  • The younger the children, the quicker they learn a new language.
  • The thinner you are, the easier it is to run.
  • The healthier your eating habits, the better your health.
  • The more careful a driver, the safer the journey.
  • The simpler one lives, the easier one's life.
  • The cleaner a country, the healthier its people.
  • The longer the days, the shorter the nights.
  • The harder the nut, the more difficult it is to break it.
  • The busier one gets, the less the time one has for oneself.

More Examples

  • The better the quality of the material, the higher the cost.
  • The older the wood, the more expensive the furniture will be.
  • The shadier the place, the cooler it will be for resting.
  • The hotter the water, the nicer the tea.
  • The plainer one's style of living, the easier one's life becomes.
  • The darker the room, the more comfortable I feel.

Mountain Climbers' Trip

The same pattern fills the climbers' passage: the nearer the day came, the more excited we got; the more organised we tried to leave, the more unorganised we seemed to get; the quicker we thought we were, the later it seemed we were; the nearer the van drew to the mountain, the brighter the look in everyone's eyes; the cooler the mountain air got, the fresher we felt; the higher we got, the more difficult it was to breathe; the quicker we tried to climb, the slower we became; the steeper we climbed, the quieter our speed became; and the nearer the end of the journey, the farther it seemed.

Key Points

  • Use 'the' before each comparative adjective in this pattern.
  • Some comparatives use 'more': more careful, more difficult, more expensive, more comfortable, more excited, more organised.
  • Some use 'less': the busier one gets, the less time one has.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: '___ the train, ___ we will reach.' (fast, soon)
options: The faster the train, the sooner we will reach
The fastest the train, the soonest we will reach
Faster the train, sooner we will reach
The fast the train, the soon we will reach
mcqs.why: The faster the train, the sooner we will reach is correct because the pattern uses 'the' with the comparative forms faster and sooner.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: '___ the children, ___ they learn a new language.' (young, quick)
options: The youngest the children, the quickest they learn
The younger the children, the quicker they learn
Younger the children, quicker they learn
The young the children, the quick they learn
mcqs.why: The younger the children, the quicker they learn is correct because younger and quicker are the comparative forms needed in the The... The... pattern.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: '___ your eating habits, ___ your health.' (healthy, good)
options: The healthy your eating habits, the good your health
The healthiest your eating habits, the best your health
The healthier your eating habits, the better your health
Healthier your eating habits, better your health
mcqs.why: The healthier your eating habits, the better your health is correct because the comparative of healthy is healthier and the comparative of good is better.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: '___ a driver, ___ the journey.' (careful, safe)
options: The careful a driver, the safe the journey
The most careful a driver, the safest the journey
Careful a driver, safe the journey
The more careful a driver, the safer the journey
mcqs.why: The more careful a driver, the safer the journey is correct because careful forms its comparative with more, while safe becomes safer.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: '___ the days, ___ the nights.' (long, short)
options: The longer the days, the shorter the nights
The longest the days, the shortest the nights
Longer the days, shorter the nights
The long the days, the short the nights
mcqs.why: The longer the days, the shorter the nights is correct because longer and shorter are the comparative forms used with 'the' on both sides.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: '___ one gets, ___ the time one has for oneself.' (busy)
options: The busiest one gets, the least time
The busier one gets, the less the time one has
Busier one gets, less time one has
The busy one gets, the little time one has
mcqs.why: The busier one gets, the less the time one has is correct because busier pairs with less to show that more work leaves less free time.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: '___ the quality of the material, ___ the cost.' (good, high)
options: The good the quality, the high the cost
The best the quality, the highest the cost
The better the quality of the material, the higher the cost
Better the quality, higher the cost
mcqs.why: The better the quality of the material, the higher the cost is correct because better is the comparative of good and higher is the comparative of high.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: '___ the wood, ___ expensive the furniture will be.' (old)
options: The old the wood, the expensive the furniture
The oldest the wood, the most expensive the furniture
Older the wood, expensive the furniture
The older the wood, the more expensive the furniture will be
mcqs.why: The older the wood, the more expensive the furniture will be is correct because older is the comparative of old and expensive needs more expensive.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: '___ the place, ___ it will be for resting.' (shady, cool)
options: The shadier the place, the cooler it will be for resting
The shadiest the place, the coolest it will be
Shadier the place, cooler it will be
The shady the place, the cool it will be
mcqs.why: The shadier the place, the cooler it will be for resting is correct because shadier and cooler are the comparative forms in the book's sentence.

mcqs.q: In the Mountain Climbers' Trip: '___ we got, ___ it was for us to breathe.' (high, difficult)
options: The highest we got, the difficult it was
The higher we got, the more difficult it was for us to breathe
Higher we got, difficult it was
The high we got, the difficulty it was
mcqs.why: The higher we got, the more difficult it was to breathe is correct because the passage uses higher with more difficult as the climbers went up the mountain.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Relative Pronouns
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Points

Relative pronouns join two parts of a sentence and refer back to a noun. Use who for people, and which or that for things and animals. In the exercises, 'that' is also used for things, houses, books, trees and ideas.

Examples with Who

  • I know the maid who broke the new tray.
  • A gold medal was given to the player who scored the most runs.
  • The woman who is wearing a blue shawl is my sister.
  • The child who was running slipped and fell.
  • Their new teacher, who sings beautifully, is absent today.
  • My grandfather who travels a lot has gone to Canada.
  • One of our neighbours who used to live with us now lives with my uncle.

Examples with Which and That

  • The farmer found the goat which had been stolen from his farm.
  • Zameer owns the shop which has five doors.
  • You will find the captain at the table which is near the window.
  • The book that has a yellow sticker belongs to Asad.
  • My friend painted the house that we sold yesterday.
  • Many birds used to nest in the tree that they cut.
  • The ice-cream that is in this tub is better.
  • It was our class team that won the volley ball match.

Dialogue Examples

Uncle Jamal who is ill; the park which is near his house; my friend who lives next door; a small hotel which serves good food; the hawker who stands outside the park; a shop which sells cone ice cream; the ice cream which has chocolate pieces in it; mother, who is busy in the kitchen; the idea that we visit uncle Jamal; the bun kebab which is sold near the park.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'I know the maid ___ broke the new tray.'
mcqs.why: Who is correct because the maid is a person, and the book's sentence is 'I know the maid who broke the new tray.'

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'A gold medal was given to the player ___ scored the most runs.'
mcqs.why: Who is correct because the player is a person who scored the most runs, so the relative pronoun for a person is used.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'The book ___ has a yellow sticker belongs to Asad.'
mcqs.why: That is correct because the book is a thing, and the book's sentence is 'The book that has a yellow sticker belongs to Asad.'

mcqs.q: Join the parts: 'The farmer found the goat...'
options: that won the volley ball match
which had been stolen from his farm
mcqs.why: Which had been stolen from his farm is correct because the goat is an animal and this part completes the farmer and goat sentence in the exercise.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'You will find the captain at the table ___ is near the window.'
mcqs.why: Which is correct because the table is a thing, and the book's sentence uses which for the table near the window.

mcqs.q: Join the parts: 'Their new teacher, ___ , is absent today.'
mcqs.why: Who sings beautifully is correct because the teacher is a person, and the joined sentence says the new teacher who sings beautifully is absent today.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'Let's go and visit uncle Jamal ___ is ill.'
mcqs.why: Who is correct because uncle Jamal is a person, and the dialogue begins with a visit to uncle Jamal who is ill.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'We can have dinner at any small hotel ___ serves good food.'
mcqs.why: Which is correct because the hotel is a place or thing in this sentence, and the dialogue uses which for the hotel that serves good food.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'Buy bun kebab from the hawker ___ stands outside the park.'
mcqs.why: Who is correct because the hawker is a person who stands outside the park, so the dialogue uses who for the hawker.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'She loved the idea ___ we visit uncle Jamal.'
mcqs.why: That is correct because idea is a thing, and the dialogue ends with the idea that we visit uncle Jamal, using that for the idea.

lessons.title: Writing: A Letter
lessons.notes_html:
Formal Letter Format

This lesson gives one model formal letter. A formal letter includes the date, the receiver's name and address, a respectful greeting, the writer's introduction, the main request, a polite closing and the writer's name.

The Model Letter

  • Date: 15 November 2017
  • To: The Minister of Sports, Ministry of Sports, Government of Sindh, Karachi
  • Greeting: Respected Sir,
  • Writer: Ahmed Khan, a student of Class VIII at Government High School, Jamshoro
  • Purpose: To inform the Minister about the need of a playground in his area

Main Points of the Letter

  • The area has more than five hundred children, but there is no playground where they can play.
  • Children play in the streets, which is dangerous because of traffic.
  • A playground will keep children healthy and safe.
  • A playground will also help children learn sportsmanship and teamwork.
  • Request: kindly arrange a playground in the area as soon as possible.

Closing

The letter closes politely with "I shall be very thankful to you for your kind action" and "Thanking you in anticipation." It is signed: Yours faithfully, Ahmed Khan.

mcqs.q: To whom is the model letter written?
options: The captain of the cricket team
mcqs.why: The Minister of Sports is correct because the letter is addressed to the Minister of Sports, Ministry of Sports, Government of Sindh, Karachi.

mcqs.q: Who wrote the model letter?
options: Ahmed Khan, a student of Class VIII
mcqs.why: Ahmed Khan is correct because the writer introduces himself as Ahmed Khan, a student of Class VIII at Government High School, Jamshoro.

mcqs.q: Where does the writer study?
mcqs.why: Government High School, Jamshoro is correct because Ahmed Khan states his class and school clearly in the opening of the formal letter.

mcqs.q: What is the main request in the letter?
options: A library for five hundred children
A playground in the writer's area
mcqs.why: A playground in the writer's area is correct because the whole letter informs the Minister about the need of a playground and asks him to arrange one.

mcqs.q: How many children are there in the writer's area, according to the letter?
mcqs.why: More than five hundred children is correct because the letter says the area has more than five hundred children but no playground for them.

mcqs.q: Why is it dangerous for the children at present?
options: They play in the streets, which is dangerous because of traffic
They travel far for a bus
They climb mountains without a guide
mcqs.why: Playing in the streets is dangerous because of traffic, which is the reason the letter gives for why a safe playground is urgently needed.

mcqs.q: How will a playground help the children, apart from keeping them safe?
options: It will give them Rs. 200 each
It will help them win a world record
It will help them learn sportsmanship and teamwork
It will stop all traffic in the area
mcqs.why: It will help them learn sportsmanship and teamwork is correct because the letter says a playground keeps children healthy and safe and teaches these values.

mcqs.q: What date is written on the model letter?
mcqs.why: 15 November 2017 is correct because that is the date written at the top of the model formal letter to the Minister of Sports.

mcqs.q: How does the writer close the letter?
mcqs.why: Yours faithfully, Ahmed Khan is correct because a formal letter ends respectfully, and this model letter is signed in exactly that way.

mcqs.q: What does the writer request the Minister to do about timing?
options: Arrange a playground as soon as possible
Ban children from the streets only
mcqs.why: Arrange a playground as soon as possible is correct because the writer requests kind action at the earliest and thanks the Minister in anticipation.

An analogy here means forming the doer word: the person who does an action. One who sings is a singer, one who writes is a writer. Learn the full list from the exercise.

lessons.title: Fun: Playing Games
lessons.notes_html:
Fun: Playing Games - Conditional Sentences

In this game, each box gives an imaginary situation starting with If I... and the player completes a conditional sentence with what he or she would do. The model sentences use would for the result.

Model Sentences

  • If I were rich, I would help poor people.
  • If I saw a ghost, I would run away.
  • If I caught a thief, I would hand him over to the police.
  • If I were a genius, I would invent new things.
  • If I went to China, I would visit the Great Wall.
  • If I could fly, I would fly over the mountains.
  • If I failed in my exams, I would work harder next time.
  • If I were 7 ft tall, I would play basketball.
  • If I could see in the dark, I would never need a torch.
  • If I found a bag full of money, I would return it to its owner.
  • If I were the Prime Minister of Pakistan, I would build more schools.
  • If I got the top position in my exams, I would thank my teachers.
  • If I could study any subject I wanted, I would study science.
  • If I got selected for the Olympic games, I would work hard to win a medal.
  • If I could read people's minds, I would know what they think.
  • If I could be invisible, I would help people secretly.
  • If I could drive a car, I would drive my family to the picnic.
  • If I were poor, I would still work hard.
  • If I received Rs. 5000, I would buy books.
  • If I could eat whatever I wanted, I would eat ice cream every day.
  • If I were the principal of my school, I would make a big playground.
  • If I could be a clown, I would make children laugh.
  • If I could be really handsome/beautiful, I would still be kind to everyone.

Key Points

  • The situation is imaginary, so the model uses 'were' for being: If I were rich, If I were the Prime Minister.
  • The result part uses 'would' plus the action: would help, would return, would build, would buy.
