chapters.title: Unit 7: The Multiple Roles That Women Play

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: The Multiple Roles That Women Play
lessons.notes_html:
Text Summary

The main idea of the text is that women are productive members of a society. No family, society or nation can progress unless women take part in economic activity.

Arshad has been touring the province for many months, gathering information for a report he is writing. He shows Noman an interesting picture of a woman with many hands, because women do many kinds of work, sometimes all at the same time. This is called multi-tasking.

Noman's mother and grandmother are both economically active. His mother hand-weaves cloth that is sent to the city and sold. His grandmother takes orders and sells her embroidery, which is also her favourite pastime.

Word Meanings

  • development sector — a field in which progress and improvement is studied
  • hovering — stand or move about near someone without any purpose
  • seminar — a gathering of people for exchanging ideas and discussing
  • present — to share information and thought
  • chores — everyday work
  • simultaneously — at the same time
  • multi-tasking — doing two or more things at the same time
  • economic activity — work that is done to earn some money
  • weave — make cloth with thread
  • pastime — a thing done for enjoyment
  • nation-building — developing the country

Four words in the word list do not appear in the text: conference, discussion, community and issue.

Types of Work Women Do

Household ChoresFamily Income Chores at Home or in the FieldWork Outside the Home
Cooking, cleaning, taking care of the houseHand-weaving cloth, embroidery, picking cotton, plucking roses, cutting crops, milking cows and buffaloes, keeping hens and selling eggsTeachers, doctors, nurses, bank workers, office workers, store workers, factory workers

Other areas students can add themselves, which are not in the text, include engineers, police officers, lawyers and pilots.

True, False or Not Stated

  • Arshad has done a lot of travelling over the last several months — True. He has been touring the province.
  • Arshad spent a lot of time in Tharparkar — Not Stated. No place is named.
  • Arshad is writing poetry to present at the seminar — False. He is writing a report.
  • Noman's mother and grandmother are both economically active — True.
  • Education will help women become better cooks — Not Stated.
  • Women have the ability to do a number of things at the same time — True.
  • Women are as important as men for the progress and development of a country — True.
  • In cities, women work only in offices — False. They work in banks, offices, stores and factories.
  • Pakistan has many female doctors — Not Stated. The text says women work as doctors, but not how many.
  • Arshad feels that education is not important for women — False. He says women must be encouraged to acquire education.

Key Points

  • Arshad toured the province because he was gathering information for a report he was writing.
  • Noman thought his grandmother did embroidery because it was her favourite pastime.
  • Arshad believed women must acquire education because then they can become more productive members of society.
  • Girls should be encouraged to study because then they can adopt different professions if they want to.
  • Noman wanted to go to the seminar with his father because he wanted to hear more about women and how they contribute to nation-building. His father did not promise to take him because he had to ask permission from the organisers.
  • After the discussion, Arshad asked Noman to go away because he had to work on his report.

Mind Map: The Multiple Roles of Women

  • Economic activity at home: hand-weaving cloth, embroidery, keeping hens, selling eggs and milk.
  • Importance of education: educated women become more productive members of society; they spend more on children's health care and education.
  • Economic activity outside the home: teachers, doctors, nurses, bank, office, store and factory workers.
  • Helping other family members to earn more: working in fields, picking cotton, cutting crops, and supporting the family income.

mcqs.q: Which statement best describes the main idea of the text?
options: Women are useful members of their homes
Women are productive members of a society
Women stay at home, cook and clean
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that women are productive members of a society, because the text says no family, society or nation can progress unless women take part in economic activity.

mcqs.q: What does 'development sector' mean in the text?
options: A field in which progress and improvement is studied
Work done to earn some money
mcqs.why: Development sector means a field in which progress and improvement is studied, which is the meaning matched with this phrase in the vocabulary exercise.

mcqs.q: What does 'hovering' mean?
options: Standing or moving about near someone without any purpose
Doing many things at the same time
mcqs.why: Hovering means standing or moving about near someone without any purpose, as given in the word-meaning matching exercise in the text.

mcqs.q: Which word means 'a gathering of people for exchanging ideas and discussing'?
mcqs.why: A seminar is a gathering of people for exchanging ideas and discussing, which is why Arshad and Noman talk about attending a seminar in the text.

mcqs.q: What does 'chores' mean?
options: A field of progress and improvement
mcqs.why: Chores means everyday work, such as the cooking, cleaning and house care that the text lists under household chores.

mcqs.q: What does 'simultaneously' mean?
mcqs.why: Simultaneously means at the same time, which links to the picture of a woman doing many kinds of work all at once.

mcqs.q: What is 'multi-tasking'?
options: Doing two or more things at the same time
mcqs.why: Multi-tasking is doing two or more things at the same time, which is why the picture shows a woman with many hands doing many jobs.

mcqs.q: Which phrase means 'work that is done to earn some money'?
mcqs.why: Economic activity is work that is done to earn some money, and the text says women must take part in it for a nation to progress.

mcqs.q: Which four words from the list do NOT appear in the text?
mcqs.why: Conference, discussion, community and issue are the four extra words that do not appear in the text, while the other listed words are all used in it.

mcqs.q: How is the statement 'Arshad is writing poetry to present at the seminar' judged?
mcqs.why: This statement is False because Arshad is writing a report, not poetry, and he toured the province to gather information for that report.

mcqs.q: How is the statement 'Noman's mother and grandmother are both economically active' judged?
mcqs.why: This statement is True because his mother hand-weaves cloth for sale and his grandmother takes orders and sells her embroidery.

mcqs.q: How is the statement 'Education will help women become better cooks' judged?
mcqs.why: This statement is Not Stated because the text does not say this; it says education helps women become more productive members of society.

mcqs.q: Which work belongs under Household Chores in the text?
options: Cooking, cleaning and taking care of the house
Working in a bank or factory
mcqs.why: Cooking, cleaning and taking care of the house are listed as household chores, while field work and jobs outside are placed in other groups.

mcqs.q: Why were Noman's mother and grandmother economically active?
options: They worked only in offices in the city
They taught in a school together
His mother hand-wove cloth that was sold, and his grandmother took orders and sold her embroidery
They picked cotton in another province
mcqs.why: They were economically active because his mother hand-wove cloth that was sent to the city and sold, and his grandmother took orders and sold her embroidery work.

mcqs.q: Why did Arshad tour the province?
options: To present poetry at a seminar
He was gathering information for a report he was writing
To visit Tharparkar for a holiday
mcqs.why: Arshad toured the province because he was gathering information for a report he was writing, as the past-tense completion exercise explains.

lessons.title: Speaking: Persuading with Fillers
lessons.notes_html:
About This Lesson

This is a thin lesson based on one model dialogue only. Noman talks to his sister Maleeha, who is 10 years old. Maleeha plays the whole day, hardly does her homework, rarely goes to school and gets bad grades. Noman persuades her to take her studies seriously so that she can play an important and productive role in society.

What Are Fillers?

Fillers are small words and phrases speakers use in natural conversation while speaking and persuading. The fillers used in this dialogue are:

  • you know
  • like
  • ok
  • well
  • basically
  • literally
  • actually
  • oh really
  • to tell you the truth
  • you see

The Model Dialogue

  • Noman: Maleeha, where have you been? It's almost sunset.
  • Maleeha: Oh, I was at Seema's house.
  • Noman: Well, you know, you play the whole day and hardly ever do your homework.
  • Maleeha: Oh really? But I like playing.
  • Noman: To tell you the truth, playing all day will not help you in the future. You see, if you study well, you can become a teacher or a doctor.
  • Maleeha: Actually, I don't like studying.
  • Noman: Well, basically, studying is the key to a good future. If you study, you can play an important and productive role in society.
  • Maleeha: Ok, I will try to study every day and do my homework.
  • Noman: That's great! I will help you with your studies.

Key Points

  • Noman persuades gently. He does not scold Maleeha; he explains the future benefit of studying.
  • Studying well can lead Maleeha to become a teacher or a doctor.
  • At the end, Maleeha agrees to study every day and do her homework, and Noman offers to help her.

mcqs.q: Who is Maleeha in the dialogue?
options: Noman's sister, who is 10 years old
mcqs.why: Maleeha is Noman's sister, who is 10 years old, and Noman persuades her in the dialogue to take her studies seriously.

mcqs.q: What problem does Maleeha have with her studies?
options: She studies all day and never plays
She has no books at home
She plays the whole day, hardly does homework, rarely goes to school and gets bad grades
She goes to school but dislikes sports
mcqs.why: Maleeha plays the whole day, hardly does homework, rarely goes to school and gets bad grades, which is why Noman talks to her.

mcqs.q: Where had Maleeha been when Noman asked her?
mcqs.why: Maleeha says she was at Seema's house, in reply to Noman asking where she had been when it was almost sunset.

mcqs.q: Which filler does Noman use when he says playing all day will not help her in the future?
mcqs.why: Noman begins that honest warning with 'To tell you the truth', before explaining that playing all day will not help Maleeha in the future.

mcqs.q: What does Maleeha say when Noman tells her she hardly does her homework?
options: Oh really? But I like playing
Ok, I will study every day
You see, I was at school
mcqs.why: Maleeha replies 'Oh really? But I like playing', using the filler 'oh really' to show surprise while defending her playing.

mcqs.q: According to Noman, what can Maleeha become if she studies well?
mcqs.why: Noman says, 'You see, if you study well, you can become a teacher or a doctor', linking study to a productive future role.

mcqs.q: Which filler does Maleeha use to admit she does not like studying?
mcqs.why: Maleeha says 'Actually, I don't like studying', using 'actually' before honestly admitting her dislike of studying.

mcqs.q: How does Noman describe studying in the dialogue?
options: As harder than playing all day
As the key to a good future
mcqs.why: Noman says, 'Well, basically, studying is the key to a good future', using 'basically' to state his main point about studying.

mcqs.q: What does Maleeha agree to do at the end of the dialogue?
options: Study every day and do her homework
mcqs.why: Maleeha agrees, 'Ok, I will try to study every day and do my homework', showing that Noman's persuasion has succeeded.

mcqs.q: What does Noman offer at the end of the dialogue?
options: To take her to a seminar
To help her with her studies
To do all her homework for her
mcqs.why: Noman offers to help her with her studies, saying 'That's great! I will help you with your studies', after Maleeha agrees to study.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Adjectives with 'Than'
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Points

To compare two things, we use the comparative form of an adjective followed by than. Example: Today the weather was cooler than it was yesterday.

  • Short adjectives usually add -er: cheap — cheaper, clean — cleaner, bright — brighter, busy — busier, pretty — prettier.
  • Long adjectives use more: more intelligent, more useful, more expensive, more beautiful, more sour.
  • Irregular forms: good — better, bad — worse.

Examples from the Exercises

  • Our new neighbours are better than the older ones.
  • His boss is kinder than our boss.
  • Travelling by train is cheaper than travelling by air.
  • Your dress is prettier than your friend's dress.
  • Some students are more intelligent than the others.
  • Today the patient's condition is worse than yesterday.
  • This week has been busier than last week.
  • The elephant is bigger than the rabbit. The rabbit is smaller than the elephant.
  • The mango is sweeter than the orange. The orange is more sour than the mango.
  • The train is slower than the aeroplane. The aeroplane is faster than the train.

Comparing the Timbo and Chucky Families

FactTimbo FamilyChucky Family
Family size46
Males / Females2 / 23 / 3
Mr. — height and age5 ft 8 in, 30 years6 ft 4 in, 45 years
Mrs. — height and age5 ft 8 in, 27 years5 ft 2 in, 40 years
Children24
House2 bedrooms, built 19784 bedrooms, built 1995
Income per monthRs 20,000Rs 80,000

The Timbo family is smaller, poorer and has fewer children than the Chucky family. Mr. Timbo is shorter and younger than Mr. Chucky. Mrs. Timbo is taller than Mrs. Chucky but younger than her. The Chucky house is larger and newer than the Timbo house, and the Chucky family is richer than the Timbo family.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: Our new neighbours are ___ the older ones. (good)
mcqs.why: The comparative of 'good' is 'better', so the sentence is 'are better than the older ones', using the irregular comparative form.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: Today the patient's condition is ___ yesterday. (bad)
mcqs.why: The comparative of 'bad' is 'worse', so the patient's condition is worse than yesterday, using the irregular comparative form.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: Travelling by train is ___ travelling by air. (cheap)
mcqs.why: The comparative of the short adjective 'cheap' is 'cheaper', so travelling by train is cheaper than travelling by air.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: Some of the students in this class are ___ the others. (intelligent)
mcqs.why: Long adjectives like 'intelligent' use 'more', so some students are more intelligent than the others in the class.

mcqs.q: Which pair of sentences is correct for the elephant and the rabbit?
options: The elephant is more small than the rabbit. The rabbit is bigger than the elephant.
The elephant is bigger than the rabbit. The rabbit is smaller than the elephant.
The elephant is biggest than the rabbit. The rabbit is small than the elephant.
The elephant is big than the rabbit. The rabbit is smaller than the elephant.
mcqs.why: The elephant is bigger than the rabbit and the rabbit is smaller than the elephant, because 'big' and 'small' form comparatives with -er.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: The bag lying downstairs is ___ the one lying upstairs. (useful)
mcqs.why: Long adjectives like 'useful' use 'more', so the bag downstairs is more useful than the one lying upstairs.

mcqs.q: Which sentence correctly compares the mango and the orange?
options: The mango is sweeter than the orange. The orange is more sour than the mango.
The mango is sweet than the orange. The orange is sourer than the mango only.
The mango is more sweet than the orange only. The orange is sour than the mango.
The mango is sweetest than the orange. The orange is most sour than the mango.
mcqs.why: The mango is sweeter than the orange and the orange is more sour than the mango, using 'sweeter' for the short adjective and 'more sour' as in the book.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the Timbo and Chucky families is correct?
options: The Timbo family is bigger than the Chucky family.
The Timbo family has more children than the Chucky family.
The Timbo family is richer than the Chucky family.
The Timbo family is smaller than the Chucky family.
mcqs.why: The Timbo family is smaller than the Chucky family, with 4 members compared with 6, fewer children and a lower income.

mcqs.q: Which statement about Mr. Timbo and Mr. Chucky is correct?
options: Mr. Timbo is taller and older than Mr. Chucky.
Mr. Timbo is shorter and younger than Mr. Chucky.
Mr. Timbo is taller but younger than Mr. Chucky.
Mr. Timbo is shorter but older than Mr. Chucky.
mcqs.why: Mr. Timbo is shorter than Mr. Chucky at 5 ft 8 in against 6 ft 4 in, and younger than him at 30 years against 45 years.

mcqs.q: Which statement about Mrs. Timbo and Mrs. Chucky is correct?
options: Mrs. Timbo is taller than Mrs. Chucky but younger than her.
Mrs. Timbo is shorter and older than Mrs. Chucky.
Mrs. Timbo is taller and older than Mrs. Chucky.
Mrs. Timbo is shorter but younger than Mrs. Chucky.
mcqs.why: Mrs. Timbo is taller than Mrs. Chucky at 5 ft 8 in against 5 ft 2 in, but younger than her at 27 years against 40 years.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Pronouns and Emphatic Pronouns
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Points

A pronoun is used in place of a noun: I, you, he, she, it, we, they.

An emphatic pronoun adds emphasis and has the same form as a reflexive pronoun: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves. It shows that the person did the action personally or alone.

Examples

  • Our neighbours love gardening. They look after their plants themselves.
  • The principal, Mr. Samad, is a nice man. He himself guides all the teachers.
  • My friend gets good marks. She does not take tuitions but studies hard herself.
  • Our house is always neat and clean. We clean it ourselves.
  • All of you are loved by your teachers because you yourselves are good students.
  • Train your dog well, then it itself will take care of your house.
  • No one is responsible for your actions. Only you yourself are responsible for them.

Dialogue Examples

  • Fatima: I spoke to her last night and she herself told me that she was coming.
  • Amna: Can you try and contact her yourself to see why she is late?
  • Shirin: The teacher told us that we ourselves will be responsible for all our things.
  • Sabah: I myself typed up all the instructions of our teacher.
  • Fatima: Mr. Zameer has arranged the food. He himself will pick it up from the cook.
  • Amna: Can all of you please check if your bags have been put in the van?
  • Shirin: Those of you who will not check yourselves will be responsible if their bags are left behind.
  • Fatima: My bag is in. It went inside the van.

Key Points

  • Match the emphatic pronoun to the subject: he — himself, she — herself, we — ourselves, you — yourself / yourselves, they — themselves, it — itself.
  • Use 'yourselves' when 'you' refers to more than one person, and 'yourself' for one person.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: Our neighbours love gardening. ___ look after their plants ___.
mcqs.why: 'They themselves' is correct because the subject is 'our neighbours', a plural group, so the pronoun and emphatic pronoun must both be plural.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: The principal, Mr. Samad, is a nice man. ___ guides all the teachers.
mcqs.why: 'He himself' is correct because Mr. Samad is one man, and the emphatic pronoun 'himself' shows he personally guides all the teachers.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: My friend gets good marks. ___ does not take tuitions but studies hard ___.
mcqs.why: 'She herself' is correct in the book's answer, showing the friend is female and studies hard on her own without taking tuitions.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: Our house is always neat and clean. ___ clean it ___.
mcqs.why: 'We ourselves' is correct because the speakers include themselves in the group that cleans the house, so both forms must be first-person plural.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: All of you are loved by your teachers because ___ are good students.
mcqs.why: 'You yourselves' is correct because 'all of you' refers to more than one student, so the plural emphatic form 'yourselves' is used.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: Train your dog well, then ___ will take care of your house.
mcqs.why: 'It itself' is correct because the subject is the dog, referred to as 'it', and 'itself' adds emphasis that the dog will do it on its own.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: No one is responsible for your actions. Only ___ are responsible for them.
mcqs.why: 'You yourself' is correct because the sentence speaks to one person about his or her own actions, using the singular emphatic form.

mcqs.q: Complete Fatima's sentence: I spoke to her last night and ___ told me that she was coming.
mcqs.why: 'She herself' is correct because Fatima is reporting what Sabiha, a female, personally told her the previous night.

mcqs.q: Complete Sabah's sentence: Yes, I know. ___ typed up all the instructions of our teacher.
mcqs.why: 'I myself' is correct because Sabah is emphasising that she personally typed up all the instructions of the teacher.

mcqs.q: Complete Fatima's sentence about the food: Mr. Zameer has arranged for the food. ___ will pick it up from the cook and bring it here.
mcqs.why: 'He himself' is correct because Mr. Zameer is one man, and the emphatic form shows he will personally pick up the food from the cook.

lessons.title: Writing: An Article for the School Magazine
lessons.notes_html:
About This Lesson

This is a thin lesson based on one model article only, written for the school magazine. The article has at least four paragraphs: an introductory paragraph, two body paragraphs and a concluding paragraph.

Title

The Important Role of Women in the Development of Society

Introductory Paragraph

Women play an important role in the development of a society and nation. No family, no society and no nation can progress unless women participate in economic activity.

Body Paragraph 1: Work at Home and in the Fields

Women work at home and in the fields. They hand-weave cloth, do embroidery, pick cotton, pluck roses, cut crops, milk cows and buffaloes, and keep hens and sell eggs. In this way they add to the family income.

Body Paragraph 2: Work Outside the Home

Women also work outside the home as teachers, doctors, nurses, bank workers, office workers, store workers and factory workers. When women earn money, they usually spend it more on the health care and education of their children.

Concluding Paragraph

In conclusion, women are productive members of society. We must encourage our girls to study and adopt different professions, so that they can play their full role in the progress and development of our country.

Key Points

  • Structure to copy: introduction, body paragraph 1, body paragraph 2, conclusion.
  • The article moves from work at home and in the fields to work outside the home.
  • The conclusion returns to the main idea and gives a clear recommendation about girls' education.

mcqs.q: What is the title of the model article for the school magazine?
options: Women Who Work Only at Home
How to Write a School Magazine
The Important Role of Women in the Development of Society
mcqs.why: The model article is titled 'The Important Role of Women in the Development of Society', which states its main subject clearly.

mcqs.q: How many paragraphs does the model article have, and in what order?
options: Five: introduction, three body paragraphs, conclusion
Four: introductory, two body paragraphs and concluding
mcqs.why: The article has four paragraphs in the order introductory, two body paragraphs and concluding, as the writing task requires at least four paragraphs.

mcqs.q: What is the main point of the introductory paragraph?
options: No family, society or nation can progress unless women participate in economic activity
Women should work only in fields
mcqs.why: The introduction states that no family, no society and no nation can progress unless women participate in economic activity, which is the article's main idea.

mcqs.q: What does the first body paragraph describe?
options: Women working only as teachers and doctors
Women spending money on health care
The need to encourage girls to study
Women working at home and in the fields, adding to the family income
mcqs.why: The first body paragraph describes women working at home and in the fields and adding to the family income in this way.

mcqs.q: Which work is mentioned in the first body paragraph?
mcqs.why: Hand-weaving cloth and doing embroidery are mentioned in the first body paragraph, along with picking cotton, plucking roses and cutting crops.

mcqs.q: What does the second body paragraph describe?
options: Women working outside the home in different professions
Women keeping hens and selling eggs
mcqs.why: The second body paragraph describes women working outside the home as teachers, doctors, nurses, bank, office, store and factory workers.

mcqs.q: According to the article, when women earn money, what do they usually spend it more on?
options: The health care and education of their children
mcqs.why: The article says women usually spend their earnings more on the health care and education of their children when they earn money.

mcqs.q: How does the concluding paragraph begin?
mcqs.why: The concluding paragraph begins with 'In conclusion', and then restates that women are productive members of society.

mcqs.q: What recommendation does the conclusion give?
options: We must encourage our girls to study and adopt different professions
Women should stop working in fields
Society does not need women's work
mcqs.why: The conclusion recommends that we must encourage our girls to study and adopt different professions so they can play their full role in development.

mcqs.q: Which sentence best restates the article's conclusion about women?
options: Women are productive members of society
Women cannot help a country progress
Women should work only outside the home
mcqs.why: The conclusion restates that women are productive members of society, which is the central idea repeated from the introduction.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Abbreviations
lessons.notes_html:
